sentences.zh: 劉卞

translations.literal: Liu Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bian

sentences.zh: 鄧艾、鐘會之伐蜀也，瓘以本官持節監艾、會軍事，行鎮西軍司，給兵千人。

translations.literal: When Deng Ai and Zhong Hui campaigned against Shu, Guan, in his incumbent office, bore the credentials and supervised the military affairs of Ai and Hui, acted as army supervisor for the Army of the West, and was allotted a thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: During Deng Ai and Zhong Hui's conquest of Shu, Wei Guan kept his existing post, carried the imperial insignia, and oversaw both men's armies as acting army supervisor for the western command; the court gave him a thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 蜀既平，艾輒承制封拜。

translations.literal: Shu having been pacified, Ai then on his own authority implemented enfeoffments and appointments under mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shu had surrendered, Deng Ai began handing out titles and posts on his own authority as if the throne had authorized him.

sentences.zh: 會陰懷異志，因艾專擅，密與瓘俱奏其狀。

translations.literal: Hui secretly harbored a different purpose; because Ai acted arbitrarily, he secretly together with Guan jointly memorialized the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui nursed treason in secret; seeing Deng Ai act like a law unto himself, he slipped Wei Guan a joint memorial denouncing him.

sentences.zh: 詔使檻車徵之，會遣瓘先收艾。

translations.literal: An edict ordered them summoned in caged carts; Hui sent Guan ahead to seize Ai.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered both men brought back in prisoner carts; Zhong Hui sent Wei Guan ahead to arrest Deng Ai first.

sentences.zh: 會以瓘兵少，欲令艾殺瓘，因加艾罪。

translations.literal: Hui considered Guan's troops few and wished to have Ai kill Guan, thereby adding to Ai's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui thought Wei Guan's escort was small enough that Deng Ai might cut him down—then he could pile another charge on Ai's head.

sentences.zh: 瓘知欲危己，然不可得而距，乃夜至成都，檄艾所統諸將，稱詔收艾，其餘一無所問。

translations.literal: Guan knew they intended to endanger him, yet could not refuse; he therefore went by night to Chengdu, issued a summons to the various generals under Ai's command, stating he was acting on edict to seize Ai, and asked nothing further of anyone else.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan saw the trap but could not openly refuse. He reached Chengdu by night, sent orders to every general under Deng Ai that an edict demanded Ai's arrest, and promised to leave everyone else untouched.

sentences.zh: 若來赴官軍，爵賞如先；

translations.literal: If they come join the government army, noble rank and rewards will be as before;
translations.idiomatic: Those who rally to the imperial forces will keep their former ranks and rewards;

sentences.zh: 敢有不出，誅及三族。

translations.literal: if any dare not come forth, execution will extend to three clans.
translations.idiomatic: anyone who holds back will face execution to the third degree of kin.

sentences.zh: 比至雞鳴，悉來赴瓘，唯艾帳內在焉。

translations.literal: By the time the cock crowed, all had come to Guan; only within Ai's tent did anyone remain.
translations.idiomatic: By cockcrow every unit had reported to Wei Guan—only Deng Ai and his staff stayed inside the tent.

sentences.zh: 平旦開門，瓘乘使者車，徑入至成都殿前。

translations.literal: At dawn they opened the gates; Guan rode the envoy's carriage and went straight in to the forecourt of the Chengdu palace.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak the gates opened; Wei Guan rode the imperial courier's carriage straight to the steps of the Chengdu palace hall.

sentences.zh: 艾臥未起，父子俱被執。

translations.literal: Ai was lying down and had not risen; father and son were both seized.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai was still in bed; father and son were taken together.

sentences.zh: 艾諸將圖欲劫艾，整仗趣瓘營。

translations.literal: Ai's various generals plotted to rescue Ai by abduction; they formed ranks and hurried toward Guan's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai's officers plotted a rescue: they formed ranks and marched on Wei Guan's camp.

sentences.zh: 瓘輕出迎之，偽作表草，將申明艾事，諸將信之而止。

translations.literal: Guan went out lightly to meet them, falsely drafted a memorial expressing intention to clarify Ai's case; the generals believed him and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan rode out alone to meet them, waved a fake draft memorial promising to clear Deng Ai's name, and the generals believed him and stood down.

sentences.zh: 俄而會至，乃悉請諸將胡烈等，因執之，囚益州解舍，遂發兵反。

translations.literal: Soon Hui arrived; he then summoned all the generals including Hu Lie, seized them on the spot, imprisoned them in the Yi lodging-house, then raised troops and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui soon arrived, invited every general—including Hu Lie—into a hall, seized them all, locked them in the Yizhou hostel, and then openly rebelled.

sentences.zh: 於是士卒思歸，內外騷動，人情憂懼。

translations.literal: Thereupon the soldiers longed to return home; disturbance arose within and without; people's hearts were anxious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: The troops wanted to go home, camp and city alike were in turmoil, and fear spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 會留瓘謀議，乃書版云「欲殺胡烈等」，舉以示瓘，瓘不許，因相疑貳。

translations.literal: Hui detained Guan to plot; he wrote on a wooden slip that he 'wished to kill Hu Lie and others,' raised it to show Guan; Guan did not consent, and mutual suspicion arose.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui kept Wei Guan to plot with him, scribbled on a tablet that he meant to execute Hu Lie and the others, and held it up; Guan refused, and the two men began to mistrust each other.

sentences.zh: 瓘如廁，見胡烈故給使，使宣語三軍，言會反。

translations.literal: Guan went to relieve himself and saw Hu Lie's former attendant; he had him proclaim to the three armies that Hui had rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan slipped out to the privy, found Hu Lie's old servant, and sent him through the camps shouting that Zhong Hui had turned traitor.

sentences.zh: 會逼瓘定議，經宿不眠，各橫刀膝上。

translations.literal: Hui pressed Guan to settle the plan; they passed a night without sleep, each with a sword laid across his knees.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui pressed him for a decision; they sat up all night with swords across their knees.

sentences.zh: 在外諸軍已潛欲攻會。

translations.literal: The various armies outside already secretly intended to attack Hui.
translations.idiomatic: The troops outside were already poised to attack Zhong Hui.

sentences.zh: 瓘既不出，未敢先發。

translations.literal: Because Guan did not emerge, they did not dare strike first.
translations.idiomatic: They held back because Wei Guan had not yet come out.

sentences.zh: 會使瓘慰勞諸軍。

translations.literal: Hui ordered Guan to go comfort the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui ordered Wei Guan to go reassure the armies.

sentences.zh: 瓘心欲去，且堅其意，曰：「卿三軍主，宜自行。

translations.literal: Guan in his heart wished to leave and moreover made Hui's intention firm, saying: 'You are master of the three armies; you ought to go yourself.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan meant to escape and played along: 'You command the whole army—you should go yourself.'

sentences.zh: 」會曰：「卿監司，且先行，吾當後出。

translations.literal: Hui said: 'You are the supervising official; go first, and I shall come out afterward.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui replied: 'You are the imperial overseer—you go first; I will follow.'

sentences.zh: 」瓘便下殿。

translations.literal: Guan then descended from the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan walked straight off the dais.

sentences.zh: 會悔遣之，使呼瓘。

translations.literal: Hui regretted sending him and ordered Guan summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui immediately regretted letting him leave and sent runners to call him back.

sentences.zh: 瓘辭眩疾動，詐僕地。

translations.literal: Guan pleaded that dizziness and illness had struck him and feigned falling to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan claimed vertigo, staggered, and collapsed on purpose.

sentences.zh: 比出閣，數十信追之。

translations.literal: Before he had left the corridor, dozens of messengers pursued him.
translations.idiomatic: Before he cleared the gatehouse, dozens of messengers were chasing him.

sentences.zh: 瓘至外解，服鹽湯，大吐。

translations.literal: When Guan reached the outer lodging, he drank salt broth and vomited greatly.
translations.idiomatic: At the outer quarters he drank salt water and threw up violently.

sentences.zh: 瓘素羸，便似困篤。

translations.literal: Guan had always been frail and now seemed gravely ill.
translations.idiomatic: He had always been slight of frame; now he looked at death's door.

sentences.zh: 會遣所親人及醫視之，皆言不起，會由是無所憚。

translations.literal: Hui sent trusted men and physicians to examine him; all said he would not recover; Hui therefore had no further fears.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui sent his confidants and doctors; they all swore Guan would not rise again, so Hui relaxed his guard.

sentences.zh: 及暮，門閉，瓘作檄宣告諸軍。

translations.literal: At dusk the gates were closed; Guan drafted a proclamation and announced it to the armies.
translations.idiomatic: At nightfall the gates shut; Wei Guan drafted a call to arms and sent it to every unit.

sentences.zh: 諸軍並已唱義，陵旦共攻會。

translations.literal: The various armies had all pledged the righteous cause; at dawn they jointly attacked Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Every formation had pledged loyalty to the throne; at dawn they stormed Zhong Hui together.

sentences.zh: 會率左右距戰，諸將擊敗之，唯帳下數百人隨會繞殿而走，盡殺之。

translations.literal: Hui led his personal guard to resist; the generals defeated him; only several hundred men of his tent followed Hui circling the hall; they were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui fought with his bodyguard but the loyal generals broke him; he fled around the hall with a few hundred followers until every one of them was cut down.

sentences.zh: 瓘於是部分諸將，群情肅然。

translations.literal: Guan thereupon deployed the various generals; the crowd's mood grew orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan redeployed the commanders and order returned at once.

sentences.zh: 鄧艾本營將士復追破檻車出艾，還向成都。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers of Deng Ai's original camp again pursued and broke open the caged cart to free Ai and turned back toward Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai's old troops smashed open the prison cart, freed him, and marched back toward Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 瓘自以與會共陷艾，懼為變，又欲專誅會之功，乃遣護軍田續至綿竹，夜襲艾於三造亭，斬艾及其子忠。

translations.literal: Guan himself considered that he had joined Hui in entrapping Ai and feared mutiny; he also wished to monopolize the merit of executing Hui; he therefore sent Protector Tian Xu to Mianzhu and launched a night raid on Ai at Three Works Pavilion, beheading Ai and his son Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan knew he had helped Zhong Hui ruin Deng Ai and feared Ai might turn on him; he also wanted sole credit for crushing Hui. He sent the protector Tian Xu to Mianzhu to ambush Deng Ai at Sanzaoting by night and kill him together with his son Deng Zhong.

sentences.zh: 初，艾之入江由也，以續不進，將斬之，既而赦焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ai had entered Jiangyou, because Xu had not advanced, he was about to execute him but then pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Years before, when Deng Ai pushed through Jiangyou, Tian Xu had hung back; Ai nearly executed him but relented.

sentences.zh: 及瓘遣續，謂之曰：「可以報江由之辱矣。」

translations.literal: When Guan sent Xu, he told him: 'You may avenge the humiliation at Jiangyou.'
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Guan dispatched Tian Xu he said, 'Now you can settle the score for Jiangyou.'

sentences.zh: 事平，朝議封瓘。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, the court deliberated enfeoffing Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Once order was restored, the court debated how to reward Wei Guan.

sentences.zh: 瓘以克蜀之功，羣帥之力，二將跋扈，自取滅亡，雖運智謀，而無搴旗之效，固讓不受。

translations.literal: Guan held that the merit of conquering Shu was the collective strength of the commanders, that the two generals had been overbearing and brought about their own destruction, and that although he had employed stratagem, he had had no achievement of seizing banners; he firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan argued that Shu fell through many commanders' efforts, that Deng Ai and Zhong Hui had swaggered to their own ruin, and that his own tricks had never planted the victory banners—so he refused every prize.

sentences.zh: 除使持節、都督關中諸軍事、鎮西將軍，尋遷都督徐州諸軍事、鎮東將軍，增封菑陽侯，以余爵封弟實開陽亭侯。

translations.literal: He was appointed bearer of credentials, supervisor of military affairs of all Guanzhong, General Who Guards the West; soon transferred to supervisor of military affairs of Xu Province, General Who Guards the East, with additional enfeoffment as Marquis of Ziyang, and his surplus noble rank used to enfeoff his younger brother Shi as village marquis of Kaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: They made him credential-bearing inspector of Guanzhong armies as General Who Guards the West, then moved him to command Xuzhou as General Who Guards the East, raised his fief to Marquis of Ziyang, and used the leftover noble rank to make his brother Wei Shi village marquis of Kaiyang.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，轉征東將軍，進爵為公，都督青州諸軍事、青州刺史，加征東大將軍、青州牧。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taishi era he was transferred to General Who Conquers the East, advanced to duke, supervised military affairs of Qing Province, became Inspector of Qing Province, with additional appointment as Grand General Who Conquers the East and Shepherd of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taishi he became General Who Conquers the East and duke, commanding Qingzhou troops as inspector, then added the titles Grand General Who Conquers the East and shepherd of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 所在皆有政績。

translations.literal: Wherever he was stationed he had administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Every post he held earned a reputation for good government.

sentences.zh: 除征北大將軍、都督幽州諸軍事、幽州刺史、護烏桓校尉。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand General Who Conquers the North, supervisor of military affairs of You Province, Inspector of You Province, and Colonel Who Protects the Wuhuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Grand General Who Conquers the North, inspector of Youzhou and colonel of the Wuhuan guards.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，表立平州，後兼督之。

translations.literal: Upon reaching his post he memorialized to establish Ping Province and later concurrently supervised it.
translations.idiomatic: On taking command he memorialized to carve out Pingzhou from the frontier and later oversaw it himself.

sentences.zh: 于時幽並東有務桓，西有力微，並為邊害。

translations.literal: At that time east of You and Bing were Wu Huan and west Li Wei, both harming the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: East of Youzhou and Bingzhou stood Wuhuan chieftain Wu Huan; westward lay the powerful Li Wei—both plagued the border.

sentences.zh: 瓘離間二虜，遂致嫌隙，於是務桓降而力微以憂死。

translations.literal: Guan sowed discord between the two tribes; they came to estrangement; thereupon Wu Huan submitted while Li Wei died of anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan set the two powers against each other until they turned on one another; Wu Huan surrendered and Li Wei wasted away and died.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉其功，賜一子亭侯。

translations.literal: The court praised his merit and granted one son a village marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his service and offered one son a village marquisate.

sentences.zh: 瓘乞以封弟，未受命而卒，子密受封為亭侯。

translations.literal: Guan begged to give the enfeoffment to his younger brother; before the appointment arrived he died; his son Mi received the enfeoffment as village marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan asked to transfer the title to a brother but died before the edict arrived; his son Wei Mi received the village marquisate instead.

sentences.zh: 瓘六男無爵，悉讓二弟，遠近稱之。

translations.literal: Guan had six sons without noble rank and yielded all to two younger brothers; people far and near praised him.
translations.idiomatic: None of his six sons held titles, yet he kept passing honors to two younger brothers—people everywhere admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 累求入朝，既至，武帝善遇之，俄使旋鎮。

translations.literal: He repeatedly requested entry to court; once arrived, Emperor Wu treated him well but soon ordered him back to his command.
translations.idiomatic: He begged repeatedly for an audience in Luoyang; Emperor Wu welcomed him warmly but almost at once sent him back to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，徵拜尚書令，加侍中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianning he was summoned as Director of the Secretariat with additional attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianning he was summoned to head the Secretariat with the added title attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 性嚴整，以法禦下，視尚書若參佐，尚書郎若掾屬。

translations.literal: His nature was stern and orderly; he governed subordinates by law; he regarded the Director's office like staff aides and the secretariat gentlemen like clerks.
translations.idiomatic: He was rigid and rule-bound, ran his staff by the statute book, treated the ministry like a headquarters office, and its gentlemen like clerks.

sentences.zh: 瓘學問深博，明習文藝，與尚書郎敦煌索靖俱善草書，時人號為「一台二妙」。

translations.literal: Guan's learning was broad and deep and he was accomplished in literary arts; he and Secretariat Gentleman Suo Jing of Dunhuang were both skilled in cursive script; people of the time called them 'two marvels on one terrace.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan was deeply learned and polished in letters; he and the Dunhuang gentleman Suo Jing were masters of cursive hand—contemporaries dubbed them 'the pair of wonders on the terrace.'

sentences.zh: 漢末張芝亦善草書，論者謂「瓘得伯英筋，靖得伯英肉」。

translations.literal: At the end of Han Zhang Zhi was also skilled in cursive script; critics said 'Guan got Boying's sinews, Jing got Boying's flesh.'
translations.idiomatic: Late Han master Zhang Zhi had owned the cursive tradition; critics said Wei Guan inherited his sinews and Suo Jing his flesh.

sentences.zh: 太康初，遷司空，侍中、令如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taikang he was promoted to Minister of Works while attendant-in-ordinary and Director remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taikang he became Minister of Works while keeping his posts as attendant-in-ordinary and director.

sentences.zh: 為政清簡，甚得朝野聲譽。

translations.literal: His governance was clear and simple; he earned great reputation at court and in the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: His administration stayed lean and transparent, and court and countryside alike praised him.

sentences.zh: 武帝敕瓘第四子宣尚繁昌公主。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu ordered Guan's fourth son Xuan to marry Princess Fanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu matched Wei Guan's fourth son, Wei Xuan, with Princess Fanchang.

sentences.zh: 瓘自以諸生之胄，婚對微素，抗表固辭，不許。

translations.literal: Guan considered himself of scholar-official ancestry and that the marriage pairing was too humble; he submitted a memorial firmly declining but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan protested that his house was only scholar gentry and far beneath an imperial princess; he memorialized again and again until the throne overruled him.

sentences.zh: 又領太子少傅，加千兵百騎鼓吹之府。

translations.literal: He also held Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent with addition of a thousand household guards and a hundred riders with ceremonial drums at his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as junior tutor to the crown prince, with a thousand household guards, a hundred mounted escorts, and a full drum-and-bugle guard at his bureau.

sentences.zh: 以日蝕，瓘與太尉汝南王亮、司徒魏舒俱遜位，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Because of a solar eclipse, Guan together with Grand Commandant Prince of Runan Sima Liang and Minister of Education Wei Shu all yielded their posts; the emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: After a solar eclipse Wei Guan joined Grand Commandant Prince Sima Liang of Runan and Minister Wei Shu in offering to resign; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 瓘以魏立九品，是權時之制，非經通之道，宜復古鄉舉裏選。

translations.literal: Guan held that Wei's establishment of the nine ranks was a measure for a time of expediency, not a thorough principle; he should restore the ancient village recommendation and neighborhood selection.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan argued that the nine-rank system was a wartime stopgap, not a lasting way to choose men, and urged a return to village and neighborhood recommendations.

sentences.zh: 與太尉亮等上疏曰：「昔聖王崇賢，舉善而教，用使朝廷德讓，野無邪行。

translations.literal: Together with Grand Commandant Liang and others he submitted a memorial saying: 'In antiquity sage kings esteemed the worthy, promoted the good and instructed thereby, so that the court practiced virtue and yielding and in the wilds there was no wicked conduct.'
translations.idiomatic: He and Grand Commandant Sima Liang memorialized: 'Ancient sage-kings exalted the worthy, lifted the good, and taught the realm, so the court shone with deference and the countryside knew no evil.'

sentences.zh: 誠以閭伍之政，足以相檢，詢事考言，必得其善，人知名不可虛求，故還修其身。

translations.literal: Truly because the government of village and company was sufficient to keep one another in check, inquiring of affairs and examining words, one was sure to obtain the good; people knew that reputation could not be sought emptily, therefore they returned to cultivate themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Village organization was enough to keep people honest: ask what they had done, test what they said, and the worthy emerged. No one could fake a name, so every man polished his own conduct.

sentences.zh: 是以崇賢而俗益穆，黜惡而行彌篤。

translations.literal: Therefore by esteeming the worthy custom became more reverent, and by dismissing the wicked conduct became more sincere.
translations.idiomatic: Revere the worthy and the customs grow calm; drive out the wicked and conduct turns steadfast.

sentences.zh: 斯則鄉舉裏選者，先王之令典也。

translations.literal: This is the village recommendation and neighborhood selection: the model statutes of the former kings.
translations.idiomatic: Village and neighborhood selection was the great law of the former kings.

sentences.zh: 自茲以降，此法陵遲。

translations.literal: From this time downward, this method declined.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the method crumbled.

sentences.zh: 魏氏承顛覆之運，起喪亂之後，人士流移，考詳無地，故立九品之制，粗且為一時選用之本耳。

translations.literal: The Wei house inherited a time of overthrow, arose after mourning and chaos; gentlemen drifted and relocated; there was no place for thorough examination; therefore they established the nine-rank system, roughly serving as a foundation for selection at that time only.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei state rose amid collapse: families were scattered, no one could be vetted at home, so the nine ranks were a rough makeshift for that age alone.

sentences.zh: 其始造也，鄉邑清議，不拘爵位，褒貶所加，足為勸勵，猶有鄉論餘風。

translations.literal: At its first creation, village and district pure critique did not bind noble rank; praise and blame applied were sufficient for encouragement; there still remained surplus wind of village discussion.
translations.idiomatic: At first local opinion still mattered more than pedigree; praise and blame meant something, and something of the old village scrutiny survived.

sentences.zh: 中間漸染，遂計資定品，使天下觀望，唯以居位為貴，人棄德而忽道業，爭多少於錐刀之末，傷損風俗，其弊不細。

translations.literal: In the middle period gradual staining occurred; they then calculated pedigree to fix rank, causing all under Heaven to look toward nothing but holding office as honorable; people discarded virtue and neglected pursuit of the Way, wrangling over minute gains at the tip of an awl-point; customs were harmed and injured; the harm was not small.
translations.idiomatic: Gradually rank became a tally of pedigree; the empire learned to chase titles alone, forget virtue, haggle over petty advantage, and morale corroded—the harm was immense.

sentences.zh: 今九域同規，大化方始，臣等以為宜皆蕩除末法，一擬古制，以土斷，定自公卿以下，皆以所居為正，無復懸客遠屬異土者。

translations.literal: Now the nine regions share one norm and great transformation has just begun; we your servants consider it fitting entirely to sweep away the decadent methods, unify on ancient institutions, use soil-bound registration; fixing from dukes and ministers downward all take residence as correct; no longer have detached guests remotely affiliated with alien lands.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is reuniting and great renewal begins—we urge wiping away these decadent rules and anchoring everyone to the ancient model: register people where they live, from the highest minister to the meanest clerk, and end hollow domiciles in distant commanderies.

sentences.zh: 如此，則同鄉鄰伍，皆為邑裏，郡縣之宰，即以居長，盡除中正九品之制，使舉善進才，各由鄉論。

translations.literal: In this way then same-village and neighboring company all become town and village; the shepherds of commanderies and districts will take the local head; entirely remove the system of rectifiers and nine ranks, causing promotion of good and advancement of talent each to follow village discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Then every neighborhood becomes a true community, magistrates work with the heads of residence, the rectifiers and nine ranks vanish, and good men rise through local opinion again.

sentences.zh: 然則下敬其上，人安其教，俗與政俱清，化與法並濟。

translations.literal: Then inferiors respect superiors; people find peace in instruction; custom and government together are pure; transformation and law jointly succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Inferiors would honor superiors, people would trust instruction, morals and policy would both clarify, and culture would march with law.

sentences.zh: 人知善否之教，不在交遊，即華競自息，各求於己矣。

translations.literal: People will know that teaching of good and bad lies not in socializing; then vain rivalry will of itself cease; each will seek it in himself.
translations.idiomatic: Once everyone sees character is not won by networking, empty rivalry dies and each man looks to himself.

sentences.zh: 今除九品，則宜准古制，使朝臣共相舉任，於出才之路既博，且可以厲進賢之公心，核在位之明暗，誠令典也。

translations.literal: Now if we abolish the nine ranks, then it is fitting to align with ancient institutions, causing court ministers mutually to recommend appointments; the roads for producing talent will be broad, and moreover one can encourage the impartial heart that advances the worthy, examine the brightness or darkness of those in office; truly it is a proper model.
translations.idiomatic: Scrap the nine ranks and follow antiquity: let ministers recommend one another openly. Talent will find many paths, the throne can spur honest promotion, and measure who shines or fails in office—that would be a worthy statute.

sentences.zh: 」武帝善之，而卒不能改。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu praised it but in the end could not change.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu praised the plan yet never carried it out.

sentences.zh: 惠帝之為太子也，朝臣咸謂純質，不能親政事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui was heir apparent, court ministers all said he was simple and honest and could not personally attend to government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Zhong was named heir, officials whispered that he was too simple to rule.

sentences.zh: 瓘每欲陳啟廢之，而未敢發。

translations.literal: Guan repeatedly wished to memorialize proposing his deposition but did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan often meant to memorialize for his removal but held his tongue.

sentences.zh: 後會宴陵雲臺，瓘託醉，因跪帝床前曰：「臣欲有所啟。

translations.literal: Later when there was a banquet at Lingyun Terrace, Guan pretended drunkenness and knelt before the emperor's couch saying: 'Your servant wishes to memorialize something.'
translations.idiomatic: Later, at a banquet on Lingyun Terrace, Wei Guan feigned drunkenness, knelt by the emperor's couch, and said, 'I must speak.'

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「公所言何耶？

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'What is it that you say, lord?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, 'What is it, Minister?'

sentences.zh: 」瓘欲言而止者三，因以手撫床曰：「此座可惜！

translations.literal: Guan wished to speak but stopped three times; then with his hand stroked the couch saying: 'This seat is regrettable!'
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan started and stopped three times, then stroked the couch and cried, 'What a waste of this seat!'

sentences.zh: 」帝意乃悟，因謬曰：「公真大醉耶？

translations.literal: The emperor's intention then understood; therefore falsely said: 'Are you truly greatly drunk, lord?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor caught his meaning and covered with a laugh: 'You are truly drunk, are you not?'

sentences.zh: 」瓘於此不復有言。

translations.literal: Guan at this point had no further words.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan said nothing more.

sentences.zh: 賈后由是怨瓘。

translations.literal: Empress Jia therefore resented Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia nursed a grudge from that day on.

sentences.zh: 宣尚公主，數有酒色之過。

translations.literal: Xuan had married the princess and repeatedly had faults of wine and sex.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xuan, now the imperial son-in-law, kept slipping into drink and dissipation.

sentences.zh: 楊駿素與瓘不平，駿復欲自專權重，宣若離婚，瓘必遜位，於是遂與黃門等毀之，諷帝奪宣公主。

translations.literal: Yang Jun had always been ill at ease with Guan; Jun further wished to monopolize power and authority; if Xuan divorced, Guan would surely yield his post; thereupon he together with the Yellow Gate and others slandered him, hinting to the emperor to strip Xuan of the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Regent Yang Jun loathed Wei Guan and meant to rule alone: divorce the princess from Wei Xuan and Guan would resign. Jun enlisted the eunuchs to slander the family until the emperor agreed to take back Princess Fanchang.

sentences.zh: 瓘慚懼，告老遜立。

translations.literal: Guan ashamed and fearful, announced old age and yielded his standing.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated and frightened, Wei Guan pleaded age and offered to step down.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔曰：「司空瓘年未致仕，而遜讓歷年，欲及神志未衰，以果本情，至真之風，實感吾心。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued saying: 'Minister of Works Guan's years have not yet reached retirement, yet he has yielded repeatedly through years; desiring while spirit and mind are not yet declined to fulfill his original intention—the wind of utmost sincerity truly moves Our heart.'
translations.idiomatic: An edict answered: 'Minister Wei Guan is not yet of retiring age, yet year after year he begs to withdraw while his mind is still sound—such steadfast sincerity moves Us deeply.'

sentences.zh: 今聽其所執，進位太保，以公就第。

translations.literal: Now We heed what he insists on, advance his rank to Grand Guardian, and let him go to his mansion as duke.
translations.idiomatic: We grant his wish: promote him to Grand Guardian and let the duke retire to his estate.'

sentences.zh: 給親兵百人，置長史、司馬、從事中郎掾屬；

translations.literal: Grant a hundred personal guards; establish chief clerk, adjutant, retainer-attendant staff;
translations.idiomatic: He keeps a hundred household guards plus chief clerk, adjutant, and secretarial staff;

sentences.zh: 及大車、官騎、麾蓋、鼓吹諸威儀，一如舊典。

translations.literal: and large carts, official riders, banners and canopies, drums and pipes—all awe-inspiring ritual forms—just as in old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: along with carriages, mounted escorts, banners, parasols, and the full drum-and-pipe escort prescribed by precedent.'

sentences.zh: 給廚田十頃、園五十畝、錢百萬、絹五百匹；

translations.literal: Grant kitchen lands ten qing, garden fifty mu, cash one million, silk five hundred bolts;
translations.idiomatic: Grant ten qing of income land, fifty mu of garden, a million cash, and five hundred bolts of silk;

sentences.zh: 床帳簟褥，主者務令優備，以稱吾崇賢之意焉。

translations.literal: bed curtains, mats and bedding—the persons in charge shall strive to make them abundantly prepared, thereby matching Our intention of esteeming the worthy.'
translations.idiomatic: bedding and mats must be of the finest weave to match Our respect for worthy ministers.'

sentences.zh: 」有司又奏收宣付廷尉，免瓘位，詔不許。

translations.literal: ' The authorities further memorialized to seize Xuan and deliver him to the Minister of Justice and to strip Guan of office; the edict did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries pressed again to jail Wei Xuan and strip Wei Guan of office; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 帝后知黃門虛構，欲還復主，而宣疾亡。

translations.literal: Later the emperor learned the Yellow Gate had fabricated; he wished to restore the princess, but Xuan died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne learned the eunuchs had lied, it meant to restore the princess to Wei Xuan—but Wei Xuan had already died.

sentences.zh: 初，杜預聞瓘殺鄧艾，言於眾曰：「伯玉其不免乎！

translations.literal: Earlier, when Du Yu heard Guan had killed Deng Ai, he said to the crowd: "Will Boyu probably not escape!"
translations.idiomatic: Long before, when Du Yu learned that Wei Guan had arranged Deng Ai's murder, he told everyone, "Boyu will not escape judgment for this."

sentences.zh: 身為名士，位居總帥，既無德音，又不御下以正，是小人而乘君子之器，當何以堪其責乎？

translations.literal: Identified as a famous scholar and occupying the rank of commander-in-chief, he had neither virtuous reputation nor governed subordinates by rectitude; he is a petty man riding the vessel of a gentleman—how shall he bear this responsibility?
translations.idiomatic: He enjoys the reputation of a leading scholar and commands whole armies, yet he leaves no virtuous word and rules his men without justice—a petty man wielding a nobleman's charge. How can he answer for that?

sentences.zh: 」瓘聞之，不俟駕而謝。

translations.literal: " When Guan heard it, without waiting for carriage he went to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan heard the verdict and went straight to Du Yu's door without waiting for his carriage.

sentences.zh: 終如預言。

translations.literal: In the end it was as Yu predicted.
translations.idiomatic: Events unfolded exactly as Du Yu had said.

sentences.zh: 初，瓘家人炊飯，墮地盡化為螺，歲餘而及禍。

translations.literal: Earlier, Guan's family cooked rice; it fell to the ground and entirely transformed into spiral shells; after more than a year the calamity reached them.
translations.idiomatic: Once, rice Wei Guan's servants had steamed spilled and turned into snails on the floor; little more than a year later disaster struck the clan.

sentences.zh: 太保主簿劉繇等冒難收瓘而葬之。

translations.literal: Grand Guardian chief clerk Liu Yao and others braved danger to collect Guan and bury him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Liu Yao of the Grand Guardian's office and others risked their lives to recover Wei Guan's body and bury it.

sentences.zh: 初，瓘為司空，時帳下督榮晦有罪，瓘斥遣之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Guan was Minister of Works, at that time tent-command supervisor Rong Hui committed an offense; Guan dismissed and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Years earlier, while Wei Guan headed the Ministry of Works, his tent-commander Rong Hui broke the law and Guan expelled him.

sentences.zh: 及難作，隨兵討瓘，故子孫皆及於禍。

translations.literal: When the calamity arose, he followed troops to attack Guan; therefore sons and grandsons all suffered the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When violence erupted Rong Hui marched with the assassins; that is why Wei Guan's sons and grandsons perished.

sentences.zh: 楚王瑋之伏誅也，瓘女與國臣書曰：「先公名諡未顯，無異凡人，每怪一國蔑然無言。

translations.literal: When Prince Chu Wei was executed, Guan's daughter wrote to court ministers saying: "My late father's name-style and posthumous title have not been made manifest—no different from common men; I always marvel that the whole state is silent."
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Sima Wei fell, Wei Guan's daughter wrote the ministers: "My father still lacks a proper posthumous honor—he might as well be any commoner—and I cannot understand how the court stays mute."

sentences.zh: 《春秋》之失，其咎安在？

translations.literal: Where lies the fault of the omissions of the Spring and Autumn?
translations.idiomatic: Where lies the blind spot that even the Spring and Autumn chroniclers condemned?"

sentences.zh: 悲憤感慨，故以示意。

translations.literal: Grieving and indignant, therefore I show my meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Grief and anger compel me to speak."

sentences.zh: 」於是繇等執黃幡，撾登聞鼓，上言曰：「初，矯詔者至，公承詔當免，即便奉送章綬，雖有兵仗，不施一刃，重敕出第，單車從命。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Yao and others held yellow banners, beat the petition drum, and memorialized saying: "Earlier, when the forgers of the edict arrived, the duke received the edict that he should be dismissed and immediately handed over seals and ribbons; although there were weapons, he did not wield a single blade; repeatedly ordered to leave the mansion, alone in a cart he obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao and his companions then raised yellow pennants, struck the petition drum, and declared: "When the forged edict arrived, the duke accepted dismissal at once, surrendered every seal and ribbon, kept his guards sheathed, and obeyed repeated orders to quit his mansion—riding out alone in a cart."

sentences.zh: 如矯詔之文唯免公官，右軍以下即承詐偽，違其本文，輒戮宰輔，不復表上，橫收公子孫輒皆行刑，賊害大臣父子九人。

translations.literal: According to the forged edict's text only the duke's office was removed; the Army of the Right downward then accepted the fraud and falsity; violating its original text, they executed chief ministers without further memorializing upward; seized the duke's sons and grandsons without authorization—all executed; villainously harmed nine men among great ministers father and son.
translations.idiomatic: The forgery removed only his offices, yet everyone below the Army of the Right treated it as genuine, ignored its wording, slaughtered chief ministers without memorializing upward, dragged away the duke's sons and grandsons, and butchered them—nine lives among the empire's most honored houses."

sentences.zh: 伏見詔書『為楚王所誑誤，非本同謀者皆弛遣』。

translations.literal: We have seen the edict text: 'Those deluded by Prince Chu who were not originally co-conspirators are all released.'
translations.idiomatic: We have seen the edict that anyone tricked by Prince Chu who was not a true conspirator should go free."

sentences.zh: 如書之旨，謂裏舍人被驅逼齎白杖者耳。

translations.literal: According to the book's meaning, it refers to lane-household men who were driven and compelled carrying white staffs only.
translations.idiomatic: That language targets only the lane runners forced to carry white staves."

sentences.zh: 律，受教殺人，不得免死。

translations.literal: By statute, receiving instruction to kill a person, one cannot be spared death.
translations.idiomatic: Statute says anyone who kills on orders still dies for it."

sentences.zh: 況乎手害功臣，賊殺忠良，雖云非謀，理所不赦。

translations.literal: How much more personally harming meritorious ministers, villainously killing the loyal and good; although it is said not to have been conspiracy, by principle it is not pardonable.
translations.idiomatic: How much less men who personally butchered honored ministers and loyal servants—even if they were not conspirators, justice cannot spare them."

sentences.zh: 今元惡雖誅，殺賊猶存。

translations.literal: Now although the chief villain has been executed, the murderous villains still survive.
translations.idiomatic: The chief villain is dead, yet his killers walk free."

sentences.zh: 臣懼有司未詳事實，或有縱漏，不加精盡，使公父子仇賊不滅，冤魂永恨，訴於穹蒼，酷痛之臣，悲於明世。

translations.literal: Your servants fear the authorities have not examined the facts in detail, or perhaps there is laxity and leakage, not adding exhaustive scrutiny, causing the duke's father-and-son enemy villains not to be extinguished; wronged souls eternally resent, appealing to the azure vault; bitterly pained ministers grieve in this enlightened age.
translations.idiomatic: We fear officials have not traced every fact and may let murderers slip away: then the duke's killers would never be punished, their ghosts would cry to Heaven forever, and loyal servants would ache under an enlightened reign."

sentences.zh: 臣等身被創痍，殯斂始訖。

translations.literal: We your servants personally suffered wounds; burial rites have only just finished.
translations.idiomatic: We ourselves bear wounds from that night; the funeral rites have barely ended."

sentences.zh: 謹條瓘前在司空時，帳下給使榮晦無情被黜，知瓘家人數、小孫名字。

translations.literal: We respectfully itemize that earlier when Guan was Minister of Works, tent attendant Rong Hui was harshly dismissed without mercy; he knew the numbers of Guan's household members and the names of young grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Rong Hui: Wei Guan cashiered him from the Ministry of Works staff, yet he knew every member of the household and each child's name."

sentences.zh: 晦後轉給右軍，其夜晦在門外揚聲大呼，宣詔免公還第。

translations.literal: Later Hui transferred to serve the Army of the Right; that night Hui outside the gate loudly shouted, proclaiming the edict releasing the duke to return to his mansion.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined the Army of the Right; that night he stood outside the gate bellowing the forged edict that dismissed the duke."

sentences.zh: 及門開，晦前到中門，復讀所齎偽詔，手取公章綬貂蟬，催公出第。

translations.literal: When the gate opened, Hui advanced to the middle gate, again read the forged edict he carried, personally took the duke's seals, ribbons, and cap ornaments, and urged the duke out of the mansion.
translations.idiomatic: When the doors opened he strode to the middle courtyard, reread the sham edict, stripped the duke of seals, ribbons, and court insignia, and drove him from the house."

sentences.zh: 晦按次錄瓘家口及其子孫，皆兵仗將送，著東亭道北圍守，一時之間，便皆斬斫。

translations.literal: Hui in order recorded Guan's household members and his sons and grandsons; all were escorted by armed troops; placed north of the road at East Pavilion under encirclement guard; in a single moment all were beheaded and hacked.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Hui then listed every dependent and child, marched them under guard to the stockade north of East Pavilion Road, and within moments cut them all down."

sentences.zh: 害公子孫，實由於晦。

translations.literal: Harming the duke's sons and grandsons was truly due to Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Hui alone slaughtered the duke's line."

sentences.zh: 及將人劫盜府庫，皆晦所為。

translations.literal: As for leading men to plunder the treasury storehouse, all was done by Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He also led the looting of the treasury."

sentences.zh: 考晦一人，眾奸皆出。

translations.literal: Examine Hui alone and the crowd of villainies all emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Question Rong Hui and every crime surfaces."

sentences.zh: 乞驗盡情偽，加以族誅。

translations.literal: We beg investigate exhaustively truth and falsity and apply clan execution.
translations.idiomatic: We beg the throne to try him fully and execute his whole clan."

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " The edict followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved."

sentences.zh: 朝廷以瓘舉門無辜受禍，乃追瓘伐蜀勳，封蘭陵郡公、增邑三千戶，諡曰成，贈假黃鉞。

translations.literal: The court considered Guan's entire household innocently suffered calamity; therefore it pursued Guan's merit in campaigning against Shu, enfeoffed him as Duke of Lanling commandery, increased fief by three thousand households, posthumous title Cheng, and gifted false yellow axe.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wei Guan's whole house had died innocent, the court posthumously credited his Shu campaign, made him Duke of Lanling with three thousand extra households, styled him "Accomplished," and awarded the ceremonial yellow axe.

sentences.zh: 恆字巨山，少辟司空齊王府，轉太子舍人、尚書郎、秘書丞、太子庶子、黃門郎。

translations.literal: Heng, courtesy name Jushan, in youth was summoned to the Prince of Qi's princely establishment under the Minister of Works; transferred to heir-apparent gentleman, secretariat gentleman, secretary vice-director, heir-apparent concubine's son attendant, and Yellow Gate gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Heng, courtesy Jushan, first served the Prince of Qi's ministry staff, then rose through heir-apparent attendant, secretariat posts, vice-director of the Palace Library, junior tutor to the heir, and gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 恆善草隸書，為《四體書勢》曰：

translations.literal: Heng was skilled in cursive and clerical script; he composed the 'Essay on the Four Scripts' saying:
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at cursive and clerical hands and wrote the Essay on the Four Scripts:

sentences.zh: 昔在黃帝，創制造物。

translations.literal: In antiquity there was the Yellow Emperor; he created and fashioned things.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of the Yellow Emperor the world first took shape through invention.

sentences.zh: 有沮誦、倉頡者，始作書契，以代結繩，蓋睹鳥跡以興思也。

translations.literal: There were Ju Song and Cang Jie; they first made written contracts to replace knotting cords; probably they observed bird tracks and arose thought.
translations.idiomatic: Scribes Ju Song and Cang Jie invented writing to replace knot records—inspiration came from watching birds' tracks in the sand.

sentences.zh: 因而遂滋，則謂之字，有六義焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon it gradually proliferated; then it was called characters; there are six meanings.
translations.idiomatic: The symbols multiplied into what we call characters, governed by six principles.

sentences.zh: 一曰指事，上、下是也。

translations.literal: First is pointing at affairs; shang and xia are examples.
translations.idiomatic: First, indicative compounds—examples are "above" and "below."

sentences.zh: 二曰象形，日、月是也。

translations.literal: Second is pictographic forms; sun and moon are examples.
translations.idiomatic: Second, pictographs—sun and moon illustrate it.

sentences.zh: 三曰形聲，江、河是也。

translations.literal: Third is form-sound; river and Yellow River are examples.
translations.idiomatic: Third, phonetic compounds—take "river" and "Ho."

sentences.zh: 四曰會意，武、信是也。

translations.literal: Fourth is combining meanings; martial and trust are examples.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, merged senses—"martial" and "trust" show how parts combine.

sentences.zh: 五曰轉注，老、考是也。

translations.literal: Fifth is mutually glossing; old and aged examination are examples.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, reciprocal glosses—"old" and "aged" interchange meanings.

sentences.zh: 六曰假借，令、長是也。

translations.literal: Sixth is borrowing; magistrate and elder are examples.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, loan characters—magistrate and elder borrow the same graphs for new sounds.

sentences.zh: 夫指事者，在上為上，在下為下。

translations.literal: As for pointing at affairs, above is above; below is below.
translations.idiomatic: Indicatives simply point: a stroke above means "up," below means "down."

sentences.zh: 象形者，日滿月虧，效其形也。

translations.literal: As for pictographic forms, sun full moon waning; they imitate their forms.
translations.idiomatic: Pictographs mimic the thing itself—the full sun, the waning moon.

sentences.zh: 形聲者，以類為形，配以聲也。

translations.literal: As for form-sound, using category as form and pairing with sound.
translations.idiomatic: Phono-semantics pair a semantic classifier with a phonetic hint.

sentences.zh: 會意者，止戈為武，人言為信也。

translations.literal: As for combining meanings, halting spear is martial; man's words are trust.
translations.idiomatic: Merged meanings join radicals: halting spears yields "martial"; person plus speech yields "trust."

sentences.zh: 轉注者，以老壽考也。

translations.literal: As for mutually glossing, by means of old longevity examination.
translations.idiomatic: Reciprocal glosses pivot around a shared root such as "old" and "examined elder."

sentences.zh: 假借者，數言同字，其聲雖異，文意一也。

translations.literal: As for borrowing, several words share the same character; their sounds although different, the written meaning is one.
translations.idiomatic: Loan usage lets one graph serve several words whose sounds differ but whose written form stays fixed.

sentences.zh: 自黃帝至三代，其文不改。

translations.literal: From the Yellow Emperor down to the Three Dynasties, the script did not change.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yellow Emperor through the Three Dynasties the ancient script stayed stable.

sentences.zh: 及秦用篆書，焚燒先典，而古文絕矣。

translations.literal: When Qin adopted seal script, burned the former classics, and ancient script was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Then Qin imposed seal script, burned the classics, and the old graphs vanished.

sentences.zh: 漢武時，魯恭王壞孔子宅，得《尚書》、《春秋》、《論語》、《孝經》。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu of Han's time, Prince Gong of Lu demolished Confucius's house and obtained the Documents, Spring and Autumn, Analects, and Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han Wudi the prince of Lu razed an old Kong mansion and found the Documents, the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Analects, and the Classic of Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 時人以不復知有古文，謂之科斗書。

translations.literal: People of the time because they no longer knew there was ancient script called it tadpole script.
translations.idiomatic: Having forgotten the ancient forms, contemporaries nicknamed the text "tadpole script."

sentences.zh: 漢世秘藏，希得見之。

translations.literal: Han-era secret treasuries; rarely obtained seeing them.
translations.idiomatic: Han libraries hoarded them; few eyes ever saw the originals.

sentences.zh: 魏初傳古文者，出於邯鄲淳。

translations.literal: At Wei inception those who transmitted ancient script came out from Handan Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Early Wei traced its paleography to Handan Chun.

sentences.zh: 恆祖敬侯寫淳《尚書》，後以示淳，而淳不別。

translations.literal: Heng's grandfather Marquis Jing copied Chun's Documents; afterward he showed it to Chun, but Chun could not distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Heng's grandfather, Marquis Jing, copied Chun's Documents version and later showed it to Chun himself—who could not tell it from his own exemplar.

sentences.zh: 至正始中，立三字石經，轉失淳法，因科斗之名，遂效其形。

translations.literal: By the Zhengshi era they erected the three-character stone classics; gradually they lost Chun's method; because of the name tadpole script, then they imitated its shape.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengshi the court carved three-graph stone classics but drifted from Chun's standard; people kept the nickname "tadpole" and carved strokes that merely looked like tadpoles.

sentences.zh: 太康元年，汲縣人盜發魏襄王塚，得策書十餘萬言。

translations.literal: In Taikang year one, people of Ji county robbed-open King Xiang of Wei's tomb and obtained bamboo documents of over a hundred thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taikang tomb robbers in Ji county opened King Xiang of Wei's grave and pulled out more than a hundred thousand words of bamboo texts.

sentences.zh: 案敬侯所書，猶有仿佛。

translations.literal: Examining what Marquis Jing wrote, there was still rough resemblance.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with Marquis Jing's copies, they still looked alike.

sentences.zh: 古書亦有數種，其一卷論楚事者最為工妙。

translations.literal: Ancient documents also had several kinds; among them one scroll discussing Chu affairs was most skillful and subtle.
translations.idiomatic: Several bundles surfaced; the scroll on Chu affairs shows the finest brushwork.

sentences.zh: 恆竊悅之，故竭愚思，以贊其美，愧不足廁前賢之作，冀以存古人之象焉。

translations.literal: Heng secretly delighted in it; therefore exhausting foolish thought, to praise its beauty; ashamed insufficient to stand beside former worthies' works; hoping thereby to preserve ancient men's forms.
translations.idiomatic: I cherish these traces and spend what wit I have to praise them, ashamed to rank beside older masters yet hoping to preserve something of antiquity's shapes.

sentences.zh: 古無別名，謂之字勢云。

translations.literal: Antiquity had no separate name; it called them graph configurations.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients had no separate term—they simply spoke of the "configuration of the characters."

sentences.zh: 「黃帝之史，沮誦、倉頡，眺彼鳥跡，始作書契。

translations.literal: "The Yellow Emperor's scribes Ju Song and Cang Jie gazed at those bird tracks and first made written contracts.
translations.idiomatic: "The Yellow Emperor's clerks Ju Song and Cang Jie watched birds' footprints and first carved true writing."

sentences.zh: 紀綱萬事，垂法立制，帝典用宣，質文著世。

translations.literal: They regulated the myriad affairs, handed down models and established institutions; imperial canons were used to proclaim; substance and pattern displayed in the age.
translations.idiomatic: They ordered the myriad affairs, fixed laws and ritual, spread the sovereign's canon, and let substance and ornament instruct the world."

sentences.zh: 爰暨暴秦，滔天作戾，大道既泯，古文亦滅。

translations.literal: Then came violent Qin, flooding Heaven with cruelty; the great Way already vanished; ancient script also perished.
translations.idiomatic: Then ruthless Qin drowned heaven in cruelty: the great Dao vanished and ancient script perished with it."

sentences.zh: 魏文好古，世傳丘墳，歷代莫發，真偽靡分。

translations.literal: Wei Wen loved antiquity; the age transmitted hill tombs; successive dynasties did not unearth them; true and false could not be divided.
translations.idiomatic: Wei antiquarians treasured old texts said to sleep in burial mounds, yet generations never opened them—nobody could tell authentic from fake."

sentences.zh: 大晉開元，弘道敷訓，天垂其象，地耀其文。

translations.literal: Great Jin opened primordial beginnings; it enlarged the Way and spread teaching; Heaven suspended its images; Earth radiates its patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Great Jin now opens an era, spreads the teaching, lets Heaven display omens and Earth shine with pattern."

sentences.zh: 其文乃耀，粲矣其章，因聲會意，類物有方：日處君而盈其度，月執臣而虧其旁，雲委蛇而上布，星離離以舒光；

translations.literal: Its patterns then shine; brilliant indeed its chapters; joining sound and combining meaning; categorizing things has method: sun occupies lord and fills its measure; moon holds minister and wanes at its side; clouds wind-coil and spread upward; stars scattered scattered extend light;
translations.idiomatic: Those graphs blaze—radiant chapters—phonetic and semantic at once: the sun stands regent and fills its disk; the moon serves as minister and thins at the rim; clouds coil upward; stars scatter their light;"

sentences.zh: 禾卉苯䔿以垂穎，山嶽峨嵯而連岡；

translations.literal: grain plants lush-lush hang ears; mountains lofty-lofty link ridges;
translations.idiomatic: grain sprays heavy ears; mountains pile ridge on ridge;"

sentences.zh: 蟲跂跂其若動，鳥似飛而未揚。

translations.literal: insects lift-lift as if moving; birds seem flying yet have not risen.
translations.idiomatic: insects seem poised to twitch; birds hover short of flight."

sentences.zh: 觀其錯筆綴墨，用心精專。

translations.literal: Observe its misplaced brush linking ink; mind employed refined and concentrated.
translations.idiomatic: Watch how brush meets ink—every stroke driven by utter focus."

sentences.zh: 勢和體均，發止無間。

translations.literal: Momentum harmonious body even; departure and stop without gap.
translations.idiomatic: Momentum balances the form; motion starts and stops without seam."

sentences.zh: 或守正循檢，矩折規旋。

translations.literal: Some guard rectitude and follow measure; square bends compass circles.
translations.idiomatic: Some strokes stand square on the guideline; compasses turn and squares fold."

sentences.zh: 或方員靡則，因事制權。

translations.literal: Some square round without rule; according to affair determine expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Others bend round and square as each shape demands."

sentences.zh: 其曲如弓，其直如弦。

translations.literal: Its curves like bows; its straightness like strings.
translations.idiomatic: Curves flex like bow limbs; straight lines hum like bowstrings."

sentences.zh: 矯然特出，若龍騰於川。

translations.literal: Proudly outstanding; as if dragons leaping in streams.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a stroke rears like dragons vaulting a river."

sentences.zh: 森爾下頹，若雨墜於天。

translations.literal: Dense-thus downward collapsing; as if rain falling from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Then dense drops plunge like rain sheeting from the sky."

sentences.zh: 或引筆奮力，若鴻雁高飛，邈邈翩翩。

translations.literal: Some draw brush exerting force; as if wild geese flying high, distant-distant flutter-flutter.
translations.idiomatic: Some lifts surge like wild geese climbing, wide and wheeling."

sentences.zh: 或縱肆阿那，若流蘇懸羽，靡靡綿綿。

translations.literal: Some unrestrained swaying-graceful; as if tassels hanging feathers, trailing-trailing continuous.
translations.idiomatic: Others drift soft as knotted tassels and hanging plumes, endlessly fine."

sentences.zh: 是故遠而望之，若翔風厲水，清波漪漣。

translations.literal: Therefore from afar gazing at it; as if soaring wind cutting water, clear waves rippling ripples.
translations.idiomatic: Step back: it is wind skimming water, bright ripples widening ring on ring."

sentences.zh: 就而察之，有若自然。

translations.literal: Approaching and examining it; it seems like nature.
translations.idiomatic: Step close: every line feels utterly spontaneous."

sentences.zh: 信黃唐之遺跡，為六藝之範先。

translations.literal: Truly traces of Huang-Tang; for the Six Arts a model ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: These are the footprints of high antiquity and the forebear of the Six Classics."

sentences.zh: 籀篆蓋其子孫，隸草乃其曾玄。

translations.literal: Zhou and seal scripts are probably its children and grandchildren; clerical and cursive are then its great-great descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and seal scripts descend as children; clerical and cursive hands are the distant great-grandchildren."

sentences.zh: 睹物象以致思，非言辭之可宣。」

translations.literal: Viewing thing-images to extend thought; not what words can proclaim."
translations.idiomatic: They summon images beyond speech—no tongue can exhaust them."

sentences.zh: 昔周宣王時，史籀始著《大篆》十五篇，或與古同，或與古異，世謂之籀書者也。

translations.literal: In antiquity in King Xuan of Zhou's time, Historian Zhou first composed the Great Seal in fifteen chapters; some same as antiquity, some different from antiquity; the age calls it Zhou script.
translations.idiomatic: Under King Xuan of Zhou the scribe Zhou wrote fifteen chapters of large seal script—some graphs match older forms, some differ—hence the style called Zhou script.

sentences.zh: 及平王東遷，諸侯力政，家殊國異，而文字乖形。

translations.literal: When King Ping moved east, regional lords practiced forceful government; households differed and states differed; written characters deviated in form.
translations.idiomatic: After King Ping moved east, warlords carved up the realm: every state wrote its own way and characters drifted apart.

sentences.zh: 秦始皇帝初兼天下。

translations.literal: The First Emperor of Qin at first united all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Then the First Emperor united the empire.

sentences.zh: 丞相李斯乃奏益之，罷不合秦文者，斯作《倉頡篇》，中車府令趙高作《爰曆篇》，太史令胡毋敬作《博學篇》，皆取史籀大篆，或頗省改，所謂小篆者。

translations.literal: Chancellor Li Si then memorialized to augment it, abolishing what did not match Qin script; Si composed the Cang Jie primer, Palace Chariot Prefect Zhao Gao composed the Yuanli primer, Grand Historian Hu Wu Jing composed the Boxue primer; all took Historian Zhou's great seal, some somewhat reduced and altered—what is called small seal.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Li Si standardized the graphs, dropped anything that defied Qin usage, and compiled the Cang Jie primer; Zhao Gao of the chariot office wrote Yuanli; Grand Historian Hu Wujing wrote Boxue—all trimming Zhou's large seal into what we call small seal.

sentences.zh: 或曰，下土人程邈為衙獄吏，得罪始皇，幽繫雲陽十年，從獄中作大篆，少者增益，多者損減，方者使員，員者使方，奏之始皇。

translations.literal: Some say the man of lower earth Cheng Miao was a yamen prison clerk; he offended the First Emperor and was imprisoned at Yunyang ten years; from prison he made large seal; where few increased, where many decreased; square ones made round; round ones made square; memorialized it to the First Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Others tell of Cheng Miao, a county clerk who angered the First Emperor and spent ten years in Yunyang prison, refashioning large seal—adding strokes where they were few, shaving them where many, squaring rounds and rounding squares—then presenting the result.

sentences.zh: 始皇善之，出以為御史，使定書。

translations.literal: The First Emperor deemed it good; released him to be imperial clerk and ordered him to fix writing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved, freed him, named him an imperial clerk, and charged him with fixing the script.

sentences.zh: 或曰，邈所定乃隸字也。

translations.literal: Some say what Miao fixed was clerical characters.
translations.idiomatic: Some say Cheng Miao's version became the clerical hand.

sentences.zh: 自秦壞古文，有八體，一曰大篆，二曰小篆，三曰刻符，四曰蟲書，五曰摹印，六曰署書，七曰殳書，八曰隸書。

translations.literal: From Qin destroying ancient script, there were eight styles: first called great seal; second small seal; third engraved tally; fourth insect script; fifth seal carving; sixth header script; seventh halberd script; eighth clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Once Qin shattered old seal traditions eight styles appeared: large seal, small seal, engraved tallies, insect motifs, seal impressions, heading labels, halberd inscriptions, and clerical script.

sentences.zh: 王莽時，使司空甄豐校文字部，改定古文，復有六書。

translations.literal: In Wang Mang's time he ordered Minister of Works Zhen Feng to collate the script sections, revise and fix ancient script; again there were six writings.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang had Minister Zhen Feng collate the lexicons and redefine ancient graphs, producing six categories.

sentences.zh: 一曰古文，孔氏壁中書也。

translations.literal: First called ancient script: the Kong clan wall documents.
translations.idiomatic: First, ancient script—the texts from Confucius's wall.

sentences.zh: 二曰奇字，即古文而異者也。

translations.literal: Second called strange characters: that is ancient script but divergent.
translations.idiomatic: Second, odd graphs—archaic forms that diverge slightly.

sentences.zh: 三曰篆書，秦篆書也。

translations.literal: Third called seal script: Qin seal script.
translations.idiomatic: Third, seal script—the Qin court standard.

sentences.zh: 四曰佐書，即隸書也。

translations.literal: Fourth called assisting script: that is clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, auxiliary script—meaning clerical.

sentences.zh: 五曰繆篆，所以摹印也。

translations.literal: Fifth called twisted seal: by means of which seal carving.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, twisted seal—used for chops and seals.

sentences.zh: 六曰鳥書，所以書幡信也。

translations.literal: Sixth called bird script: by means of which banner credentials are written.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, bird script—for banners and credentials.

sentences.zh: 及許慎撰《說文》，用篆書為正，以為體例，最可得而論也。

translations.literal: When Xu Shen compiled Shuowen, using seal script as standard, taking it as stylistic rule, most can be obtained and discussed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Shen compiled the Shuowen he took seal forms as authoritative—still the clearest framework for discussion.

sentences.zh: 秦時李斯號為二篆，諸山及銅人銘皆斯書也。

translations.literal: In Qin times Li Si was titled master of the two seal scripts; mountain steles and bronze-man inscriptions were all Si's writing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qin, Li Si was hailed as the twin-master of seal styles; every sacred peak inscription and bronze giant bore his brush.

sentences.zh: 漢建初中，扶風曹喜少異於斯，而亦稱善。

translations.literal: In Han Jianchu period, Fufeng Cao Xi slightly differed from Si but was also called excellent.
translations.idiomatic: During Eastern Han's Jianchu era Cao Xi of Fufeng tweaked Li Si's manner yet still ranked among the finest.

sentences.zh: 邯鄲淳師焉，略究其妙，韋誕師淳而不及也。

translations.literal: Handan Chun studied him, broadly penetrated his subtlety; Wei Dan studied Chun but did not reach him.
translations.idiomatic: Handan Chun studied under him and grasped the essence; Wei Dan studied Chun yet never quite matched him.

sentences.zh: 太和中，誕為武都太守，以能書，留補侍中，魏氏寶器銘題皆誕書也。

translations.literal: In Taihe era, Dan was Wudu prefect; because of ability at writing he was retained as attendant-in-ordinary; Wei house treasure vessels' inscriptions were all Dan's writing.
translations.idiomatic: During Taihe, Wei Dan governed Wudu but his calligraphy kept him at court as attendant-in-ordinary; every Wei ritual bronze carries his lettering.

sentences.zh: 漢末又有蔡邕，采斯喜之法，為古今雜形，然精密閑理不如淳也。

translations.literal: At Han end there was also Cai Yong; he gathered Si and Xi's methods, making ancient-and-modern mixed forms; however in fineness and orderly principle he did not match Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Late Han added Cai Yong, blending Li Si and Cao Xi into hybrid forms—yet his discipline never matched Handan Chun's polish.

sentences.zh: 邕作《篆勢》曰：「鳥遺跡，皇頡循。

translations.literal: Yong composed the 'Seal Momentum' saying: "Birds left tracks; the August Cang Jie followed."
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong's *Essay on Seal Momentum* begins: "Birds left their tracks; the sage Cang Jie followed."

sentences.zh: 聖作則，制斯文。

translations.literal: Sages made models; they regulated this patterning.
translations.idiomatic: Sages set the pattern and gave the world its script."

sentences.zh: 體有六，篆為真。

translations.literal: The forms are six; seal is the true one.
translations.idiomatic: Among the six styles seal script is the authentic form."

sentences.zh: 形要妙，巧入神，或龜文鍼列，櫛比龍鱗；

translations.literal: Forms are subtle, craft enters spirit; or tortoise lines needle-aligned, comb-like arrayed dragon scales;
translations.idiomatic: The shapes are subtle, the craft almost divine: some lines line up like tortoise shell cracks or dragon scales in even rows;"

sentences.zh: 紓體放尾，長短復身；

translations.literal: relax body release tail; long and short fold back on the body;
translations.idiomatic: strokes stretch and tails flare, long strokes doubling back on themselves;"

sentences.zh: 頹若黍稷之垂穎，蘊若蟲蛇之焚縕；

translations.literal: drooping like millet panicles hanging ears; winding like worms and snakes in tangled coils;
translations.idiomatic: they hang like grain ears heavy with seed, coil like serpents knotted in smoke;"

sentences.zh: 揚波振撆，鷹歭鳥震；

translations.literal: raise waves shake splinters; hawks poised birds trembling;
translations.idiomatic: waves leap and splinters fly; hawks hover while lesser birds quiver;"

sentences.zh: 延頸脅翼，勢似陵雲。

translations.literal: stretch neck tuck wings; momentum seems mounting clouds.
translations.idiomatic: necks crane and wings fold tight as if climbing through clouds."

sentences.zh: 或輕筆內投，微本濃末，若絕若連；

translations.literal: Some lightly brush inward cast; faint root thick tip; as if broken as if continuous;
translations.idiomatic: Some strokes dart inward, faint at first touch yet ink-heavy at the tip, snapping apart yet still tied together;"

sentences.zh: 似水露綠絲，凝垂下端；

translations.literal: like water dew on green silk, congealing hanging lower ends;
translations.idiomatic: like dew-beaded silk threads pooling at the hem;"

sentences.zh: 從者如懸，衡者如編；

translations.literal: followers like hanging, crosswise ones like plaiting;
translations.idiomatic: verticals hang like pendants, horizontals weave like cords;"

sentences.zh: 杳杪邪趣，不方不員；

translations.literal: dim extremities slant-trend; not square not round;
translations.idiomatic: distant tips slant off at odd angles, neither square nor round;"

sentences.zh: 若行若飛，跂歉胗胗。

translations.literal: as if walking as if flying; tip-toeing pecking pecking.
translations.idiomatic: they seem to walk or fly, to tiptoe and to peck like sparrows."

sentences.zh: 遠而望之，象鴻鵠羣游，駱驛遷延；

translations.literal: From afar gazing, they resemble swan-gooses flock swimming, relay after relay shifting extending;
translations.idiomatic: From a distance they look like wild geese gliding in long files;"

sentences.zh: 迫而視之，端際不可得見。

translations.literal: Pressing near viewing it, end limits cannot be obtained to see.
translations.idiomatic: Up close you cannot find where a stroke truly ends."

sentences.zh: 指捴不可勝原。

translations.literal: Fingertip-summation cannot exhaust tracing origin.
translations.idiomatic: No hand can chart every source."

sentences.zh: 研桑不能數其詰屈，離婁不能睹其郤間，般倕揖讓而辭巧，籀誦拱手而韜翰。

translations.literal: Yan and Sang cannot count its twists; Li Lou cannot see its gap intervals; Pan and Chui bow-yield and decline craft; Zhou recitation folds hands and sheathes brush.
translations.idiomatic: The accountants Yan and Sang cannot tally every twist; sharp-eyed Li Lou cannot spy the gaps; master artisans Pan and Chui bow away from such skill; even Historian Zhou would fold his brush in awe."

sentences.zh: 處篇籍之首目，粲斌斌其可觀。

translations.literal: It occupies the head and eye of documents; splendid blended-blended it can be viewed.
translations.idiomatic: It crowns every classic—radiant, patterned, fit to be studied."

sentences.zh: 摛華豔於紈素，為學藝之範先。

translations.literal: It spreads flower brilliance on fine silk; for learning arts it is model ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: It scatters splendor across white silk and stands first among cultured arts."

sentences.zh: 喜文德之弘懿，慍作者之莫刊。

translations.literal: It joys in patterned virtue's vast excellence; it frets that makers cannot carve it.
translations.idiomatic: I delight in how literary virtue flowers here, yet resent that no carver can fix it in stone."

sentences.zh: 思字體之俯仰，舉大略而論旃。」

translations.literal: Thinking of graph forms' bending and lifting, raising the large outline and discussing thus."
translations.idiomatic: So I ponder each stroke's rise and fall and offer this broad sketch."

sentences.zh: 秦既用篆，奏事繁多，篆字難成，即令隸人佐書，曰隸字。

translations.literal: Qin already used seal; memorial affairs were numerous; seal characters were hard to complete; they then ordered clerk people to assist writing, called clerical characters.
translations.idiomatic: Qin still wrote everything in seal script, but the paperwork swelled and seal too slow, so copyists were told to use the quick clerkly hand—hence "clerical" script.

sentences.zh: 漢因行之，獨符、印璽、幡信、題署用篆。

translations.literal: Han continued practicing it; only tallies, seals, banner credentials, and inscriptions on labels used seal.
translations.idiomatic: Han kept the practice for documents, reserving seal script for tallies, chops, banners, and public signage.

sentences.zh: 隸書者，篆之捷也。

translations.literal: Clerical script is seal's quickness.
translations.idiomatic: Clerical writing is the shortcut to seal.

sentences.zh: 上谷王次仲始作楷法。

translations.literal: Shanggu Wang Cizhong first made model method.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cizhong of Shanggu first set down the standard model.

sentences.zh: 至靈帝好書，時多能者，而師宜官為最，大則一字徑丈，小則方寸千言，甚矜其能。

translations.literal: By the time Emperor Ling loved writing, the age had many able men, but Shi Yiguan was the best; large then one character a zhang across; small then a square inch a thousand words; he greatly prided his ability.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling loved calligraphy, and many excelled, but Shi Yiguan stood first: he could write a single character a fathom wide or pack a thousand into an inch, and he flaunted the skill.

sentences.zh: 或時不持錢詣酒家飲，因書其壁，顧觀者以酬酒，討錢足而滅之。

translations.literal: Sometimes he did not bring cash but went to a wine shop to drink; thereupon he wrote on its wall; he looked to viewers to pay for wine; when the money collection was enough he effaced it.
translations.idiomatic: He would walk into a tavern penniless, cover a wall with characters, let the crowd pay his tab in exchange for the show, then erase the work once the wine was paid for.

sentences.zh: 每書輒削而焚其柎。

translations.literal: Each time he wrote he then planed and burned the models.
translations.idiomatic: After every performance he planed the wall and burned the templates so no copy survived.

sentences.zh: 梁鵠乃益為版而飲之酒，候其醉而竊其柎。

translations.literal: Liang Hu then added boards and gave him drink; waited until he was drunk and stole his models.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Hu set up extra panels, plied him with wine, and when he was drunk stole the rubbings.

sentences.zh: 鵠卒以書至選部尚書。

translations.literal: Hu in the end by writing reached Director of the Selection Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Hu rode that skill to the directorship of the Selection Bureau.

sentences.zh: 宜官後為袁術將，今钜鹿宋子有《耿球碑》，是術所立，其書甚工，云是宜官也。

translations.literal: Yiguan later became Yuan Shu's general; now in Julu Songzi there is the Geng Qiu stele, which Shu erected; its writing is very fine; it is said to be Yiguan's.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan later served Yuan Shu; the Geng Qiu stele at Songzi in Julu, raised by Shu, is thought to be his work and is superbly cut.

sentences.zh: 梁鵠奔劉表，魏武帝破荊州，募求鵠。

translations.literal: Liang Hu fled to Liu Biao; Emperor Wu of Wei broke Jingzhou and recruited seeking Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Hu fled to Liu Biao; when Cao Cao took Jingzhou he put a price on finding him.

sentences.zh: 鵠之為選部也，魏武欲為洛陽令，而以為北部尉，故懼而自縛詣門，署軍假司馬；

translations.literal: When Hu was in the Selection Bureau, Wei Wu wanted to be Luoyang magistrate but was made northern district captain; therefore in fear he bound himself and came to the gate, was assigned army acting major;
translations.idiomatic: Later, while Liang Hu oversaw appointments, Cao Cao had petitioned for the Luoyang magistracy but was offered only the northern district captaincy—so he appeared bound at Liang's gate and accepted an acting staff-major posting.

sentences.zh: 在秘書以勤書自效，是以今者多有鵠手跡。

translations.literal: In the Secretariat he by diligent writing proved loyalty; therefore now there are many of Hu's handwritten traces.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his keep in the Palace Library by copying documents, which is why so many of his autographs survive.

sentences.zh: 魏武帝懸著帳中，及以釘壁玩之，以為勝宜官。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei hung them in his tent and also nailed them on walls to enjoy; he considered them superior to Yiguan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao pinned Liang Hu's sheets inside his tent and on palace walls, judging them finer than Shi Yiguan's.

sentences.zh: 今宮殿題署多是鵠篆。

translations.literal: Now palace hall inscriptions are mostly Hu seal.
translations.idiomatic: Most palace plaques today still show Liang Hu's seal hand.

sentences.zh: 鵠宜為大字，邯鄲淳宜為小字。

translations.literal: Hu is suited for large characters; Handan Chun is suited for small characters.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Hu owned large characters; Handan Chun owned small ones.

sentences.zh: 鵠謂淳得次仲法，然鵠之用筆盡其勢矣。

translations.literal: Hu said Chun obtained Cizhong's method; however Hu's use of brush exhausted its momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Hu conceded that Chun had Wang Cizhong's method, yet his own brush exploited every ounce of momentum.

sentences.zh: 鵠弟子毛弘教于秘書，今八分皆弘法也。

translations.literal: Hu's disciple Mao Hong taught in the Secretariat; now eight-part script is all Hong's dharma.
translations.idiomatic: His pupil Mao Hong taught in the Library—today's eight-stroke clerical style follows Mao Hong.

sentences.zh: 漢末有左子邑，小與淳鵠不同，然亦有名。

translations.literal: At Han end there was Zuo Ziyi; slightly different from Chun and Hu; however also had fame.
translations.idiomatic: Late Han also produced Zuo Ziyi—his small script diverged slightly from Chun and Hu but earned renown.

sentences.zh: 魏初有鍾胡二家為行書法，俱學之于劉德升，而鍾氏小異，然亦各有巧，今大行於世云。

translations.literal: At Wei inception there were Zhong and Hu two houses making running-script method; both studied it from Liu Desheng; but the Zhong clan slightly differed; however each also had its skill; now greatly practiced in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Early Wei saw Zhong Yao and Hu Zhao define running script; both studied under Liu Desheng, Zhong's manner diverged a little, yet each had its genius—the style now dominates the realm.

sentences.zh: 作《隸勢》曰：「鳥跡之變，乃惟佐隸。

translations.literal: He composed the 'Clerical Momentum' saying: "Bird tracks' transformation is only assisting clerks."
translations.idiomatic: He titled his essay *Clerical Momentum*: "Bird tracks evolved into the clerks' assisting hand."

sentences.zh: 蠲彼繁文，崇此簡易。

translations.literal: Remove those elaborate patterns; esteem this simplicity ease.
translations.idiomatic: It sheds ornate seal curls for blunt simplicity."

sentences.zh: 厥用既弘，體象有度。

translations.literal: Its use already vast; body-images have measure.
translations.idiomatic: Once everywhere adopted, its shapes obey fixed measures."

sentences.zh: 煥若星陳，鬱若雲布。

translations.literal: Brilliant like stars arrayed; luxuriant like clouds spread.
translations.idiomatic: Bright as constellations ranged; lush as clouds piled layer on layer."

sentences.zh: 其大徑尋，細不容發。

translations.literal: Its large spans eight chi; fine does not accommodate a hair.
translations.idiomatic: The boldest strokes span eight feet; the finest wedge a hair's breadth."

sentences.zh: 隨事從宜，靡有常制。

translations.literal: Following affair conforming to suitability; there is no constant rule.
translations.idiomatic: Each composition bends to need—no rigid mould."

sentences.zh: 或穹隆恢廓，或櫛比針列，或砥平繩直，或蜿蜒膠戾，或長邪角趣，或規旋矩折。

translations.literal: Some vaulted vast-wide; some comb-like needle-aligned; some whetstone flat cord straight; some winding-gluing crooked; some long slant corner tending; some compass turning square bending.
translations.idiomatic: Some swell dome-high or march like comb teeth; some flatten like whetstones or stretch ruler-straight; others rear like coiling dragons or slash diagonally; still others pivot square on square."

sentences.zh: 修短相副，異體同勢。

translations.literal: Long and short mutually pair; different bodies same momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Long and short answer each other—different bodies sharing one rhythm."

sentences.zh: 奮筆輕舉，離而不絕。

translations.literal: Raise brush lightly lift; separate yet not break.
translations.idiomatic: The brush lifts lightly—strokes part yet never quite sever."

sentences.zh: 纖波濃點，錯落其間，若鍾虡設張，庭燎盡煙，嶄巖𡽱嵯，高下屬連。

translations.literal: Slender waves thick dots scattered among them; as if bell stands arrayed; courtyard torches all smoke; craggy rugged; high-low linked continuous.
translations.idiomatic: Ripples and ink dots scatter like ritual bells deployed, courtyard torches veiled in smoke, jagged cliffs stacked high and low in linked ranks."

sentences.zh: 似崇臺重宇，增雲冠山。

translations.literal: Like lofty terraces layered eaves; piled clouds crowning mountains.
translations.idiomatic: They resemble tiered towers heaped with rooflines, clouds banking atop a ridge."

sentences.zh: 遠而望之，若飛龍在天；

translations.literal: From afar gazing; as if flying dragon in Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: From afar they look like dragons wheeling in the sky;"

sentences.zh: 近而察之，心亂目眩。

translations.literal: Near and examining it; heart confused eyes dizzy.
translations.idiomatic: Up close they dizzy the eye and stagger the mind."

sentences.zh: 奇姿譎詭，不可勝原。

translations.literal: Strange forms crafty weird; cannot exhaust tracing origin.
translations.idiomatic: Their queer shapes outrun every catalogue."

sentences.zh: 研桑所不能計，宰賜所不能言。

translations.literal: What Yan and Sang cannot calculate; what Zai and Ci cannot speak.
translations.idiomatic: Not even Yan and Sang could tally them; Zai Gong and Zigong could not put them into words."

sentences.zh: 何草篆之足算，而斯文之未宣。

translations.literal: How are cursive and seal worth calculating; while this pattern is not proclaimed?
translations.idiomatic: Why dwell on counting seal or draft strokes when this mighty script still waits for praise?"

sentences.zh: 豈體大之難睹，將秘奧之不傳？

translations.literal: Is it that the body's greatness is hard to see; or will secret profundity not transmit?
translations.idiomatic: Is its grandeur too vast to see, or its secrets too deep to pass down?"

sentences.zh: 聊俯仰而詳觀，舉大較而論旃。」

translations.literal: For the moment bending and lifting and examining in detail; raising the large comparison and discussing thus."
translations.idiomatic: Here I lift and lower my gaze to study it and sketch the broad outline."

sentences.zh: 漢興而有草書，不知作者姓名。

translations.literal: Han arose and then had cursive script; one does not know the author's name.
translations.idiomatic: Cursive appeared with the Han, though nobody remembers who invented it.

sentences.zh: 至章帝時，齊相杜度號善作篇。

translations.literal: By Emperor Zhang's time, Qi chancellor Du Du was titled skilled at composing chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhang, Qi minister Du Du earned fame for entire compositions in draft script.

sentences.zh: 後有崔瑗、崔寔，亦皆稱工，杜氏殺字甚安，而書體微瘦。
