translations.literal: Later there were Cui Yuan and Cui Shi; both were also called skilled; Du clan's dot characters very steady; but script form slightly thin.
translations.idiomatic: Later came Cui Yuan and his nephew Cui Shi—both masters. Du's dots sat calmly but his frames ran lean.

sentences.zh: 崔氏甚得筆勢，而結字小疏。

translations.literal: The Cui clan greatly obtained brush momentum; but knotting characters somewhat sparse.
translations.idiomatic: The Cuis wielded thrilling strokes yet spaced their characters a touch loosely.

sentences.zh: 弘農張伯英者，因而轉精甚巧。

translations.literal: Hongnong Zhang Boying; thereby turning refined very clever.
translations.idiomatic: Then Zhang Boying of Hongnong refined the art into something finer still.

sentences.zh: 凡家之衣帛，必書而後練之。

translations.literal: Whenever family's silk cloth; always wrote then boiled it.
translations.idiomatic: His household bolted every roll of silk—practice writing on it before dyeing.

sentences.zh: 臨池學書，池水盡黑。

translations.literal: Facing pond studying writing; pond water entirely black.
translations.idiomatic: He practiced beside the pond until the water turned ink-black.

sentences.zh: 下筆必為楷則，號匆匆不暇草書，寸紙不見遺，至今世尤寶其書，韋仲將謂之草聖。

translations.literal: Setting brush always made model rule; called hurried-hastened no leisure for cursive; inch paper not seen discarded; down to today the age especially treasures his writing; Wei Zhongjiang called him cursive sage.
translations.idiomatic: Every stroke stayed within canonical bounds—people mocked "too busy for real cursive"—yet not an inch of paper survived unused. Posterity treasures him; Wei Zhongjiang hailed him as sage of cursive.

sentences.zh: 伯英弟文舒者，次伯英。

translations.literal: Boying's younger brother Wenshu; second to Boying.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhang Chang, courtesy Wenshu, ranked just behind him.

sentences.zh: 又有姜孟穎、梁孔達，田彥和及韋仲將之徒，皆伯英弟子，有名于世，然殊不及文舒也。

translations.literal: Further there were Jiang Mengying, Liang Kongda, Tian Yanhe and Wei Zhongjiang and such; all Boying disciples; had fame in the age; however far did not reach Wenshu.
translations.idiomatic: Disciples such as Jiang Mengying, Liang Kongda, Tian Yanhe, and Wei Zhongjiang won reputations but none approached Wenshu.

sentences.zh: 羅叔景、趙元嗣者，與伯英並時，見稱於西州，而矜巧自與，眾頗惑之。

translations.literal: Luo Shujing and Zhao Yuansi; with Boying same time; seen praised in western province; but priding cleverness self-aggrandizing; crowd somewhat deluded by them.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shujing and Zhao Yuansi worked alongside Boying and enjoyed acclaim in the west, yet their flashy tricks confused casual viewers.

sentences.zh: 故英自稱「上比崔杜不足，下方羅趙有餘。

translations.literal: Therefore Ying himself called "Above comparing Cui and Du insufficient; below squaring Luo and Zhao abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Boying boasted: "Measured against Cui Yuan and Du Du I fall short; stacked beside Luo and Zhao I still have plenty to spare."

sentences.zh: 」河間張超亦有名，然雖與崔氏同州，不如伯英之得其法也。

translations.literal: " Hejian Zhang Chao also had fame; however although with Cui clan same province; not like Boying's obtaining its method.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chao of Hejian also earned renown, yet though he hailed from the same province as the Cuis he never mastered the method like Boying."

sentences.zh: 崔瑗作《草書勢》曰：「書契之興，始自頡皇。

translations.literal: Cui Yuan composed the 'Cursive Momentum' saying: "Writing contracts' rise began from Jie-huang."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuan's *Essay on Cursive Momentum* begins: "Writing began with the sage Cang Jie."

sentences.zh: 寫彼鳥跡，以定文章，爰暨末葉，典籍彌繁。

translations.literal: Transcribe those bird tracks, to fix patterned writing; down to last twigs, canons and records ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He traced bird tracks to fix the script, and down the ages books only multiplied."

sentences.zh: 時之多僻，政之多權。

translations.literal: The age's many perversities; government many expedients.
translations.idiomatic: The age grew crooked; policy veered with every crisis."

sentences.zh: 官事荒蕪，剿其墨翰。

translations.literal: Official business waste-overgrown; cut their ink brush.
translations.idiomatic: Dust piled on public desks, so men grabbed brush and ink to keep up."

sentences.zh: 惟作佐隸，舊字是刪。

translations.literal: Only making assisting clerical; old characters are deleted.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks simplified old graphs to move faster."

sentences.zh: 草書之法，蓋又簡略。

translations.literal: Cursive script's method; probably again simple abbreviated.
translations.idiomatic: Cursive pared the forms again."

sentences.zh: 應時諭指，用於卒迫。

translations.literal: Respond to moment instructing meaning; use in haste-urgency.
translations.idiomatic: It answers the moment, suits sudden emergencies."

sentences.zh: 兼功並用，愛日省力。

translations.literal: Combine work and use together; cherish day save effort.
translations.idiomatic: It saves labor and rescues precious hours."

sentences.zh: 純儉之變，豈必古式。

translations.literal: Simple frugality's transformation; how must it be ancient model?
translations.idiomatic: Thrifty change need not obey antique models."

sentences.zh: 觀其法象，俯仰有儀。

translations.literal: Observe its law-image; bending and lifting have rule.
translations.idiomatic: Watch its images rise and fall with ritual poise."

sentences.zh: 方不中矩，員不副規；

translations.literal: Square does not hit central carpenter's square; round does not match compass;
translations.idiomatic: Squares avoid the square; circles cheat the compass;"

sentences.zh: 抑左揚右，望之若崎。

translations.literal: Suppress left raise right; gazing at it seems perilous-height.
translations.idiomatic: The left stroke bows while the right soars—seen head-on they resemble sheer ridges."

sentences.zh: 竦企鳥歭，志大飛移。

translations.literal: Stand tall crane birds poised; ambition great flying shifting.
translations.idiomatic: Forms stand like cranes poised for flight, ready to vault skyward."

sentences.zh: 狡獸暴駭，將奔未馳。

translations.literal: Crafty beasts sudden-frightened; about to gallop not yet galloping.
translations.idiomatic: They start like beasts shocked midstride—not yet launched into their run."

sentences.zh: 或𪑜𪐴點𪑮，狀似連珠，絕而不離；

translations.literal: Some dotted kernels clustered dots; appearance like linked pearls; broken yet not apart;
translations.idiomatic: Some knots heap ink beads like strings of pearls—split yet still tethered;"

sentences.zh: 畜怒怫鬱，放逸生奇。

translations.literal: Stored anger pent-depressed; released wandering births strangeness.
translations.idiomatic: pent rage suddenly bursts into wildest flourish."

sentences.zh: 或淩邃惴慄，若據槁臨危；

translations.literal: Some sheer-deep fearful-trembling; as if grasping withered facing peril;
translations.idiomatic: Some hang sheer as a man gripping deadwood above a cliff;"

sentences.zh: 旁點邪附，似蜩螗挶枝。

translations.literal: Side dots slant-attached; like cicadas clutching branches.
translations.idiomatic: secondary dots cling like cicadas hugging twigs."

sentences.zh: 絕筆收勢，餘綖糾結，若杜伯揵毒緣巇，螣蛇赴穴，頭沒尾垂。

translations.literal: Broken brush gathers momentum; leftover strands tangled-knit; as if Du Bo nocked poison along precipice; soaring snake hurrying cave; head submerged tail hanging.
translations.idiomatic: When the brush lifts, trailing ligatures knot tight—like Du Bo drawing a poisoned shaft along a cliff edge, or a serpent diving head-first into its hole with tail still dangling."

sentences.zh: 是故遠而望之，漼焉若沮岑崩崖；

translations.literal: Therefore from afar gazing at it; soaked-as if marshridge collapsing cliff;
translations.idiomatic: From a distance it falls away like a sodden ridge calving into mist;"

sentences.zh: 就而察之，一畫不可移。

translations.literal: Approaching and examining it; one stroke cannot be shifted.
translations.idiomatic: Up close not one stroke may shift."

sentences.zh: 機微要妙，臨時從宜。

translations.literal: Mechanism subtle essential subtle; facing moment follow suitability.
translations.idiomatic: Minute cues steer each flourish according to need."

sentences.zh: 略舉大較，仿佛若斯。」

translations.literal: Briefly raising large comparison; seemingly thus."
translations.idiomatic: This rough sketch only hints at its likeness."

sentences.zh: 及瓘為楚王瑋所構，恆聞變，以何劭，嫂之父也，從牆孔中詣之，以問消息。

translations.literal: When Guan was framed by Prince Chu Wei, Heng heard of the crisis; because He Shao was his sister-in-law's father, he went through a hole in the wall to visit him to ask news.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing crisis break out, Wei Heng slipped through a breach in the wall to reach He Shao—his sister-in-law's father—and press him for news.

sentences.zh: 劭知而不告。

translations.literal: Shao knew but did not tell.
translations.idiomatic: He Shao kept silent.

sentences.zh: 恆還經廚下，收人正食，因而遇害。

translations.literal: Heng returned passing under the kitchen; arresting men were eating; thereupon he suffered harm.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Heng doubled back past the kitchen where guards were eating and was cut down on the spot.

sentences.zh: 後贈長水校尉，諡蘭陵貞世子。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously awarded Colonel of Changshui; posthumous title Pure Heir of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: The court later awarded him colonel of Changshui posthumously and styled him the Loyal Heir of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 二子：璪、玠。

translations.literal: Two sons: Zao and Jie.
translations.idiomatic: He left two sons: Wei Zao and Wei Jie.

sentences.zh: 子璪、玠

translations.literal: Sons Zao and Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Sons: Wei Zao and Wei Jie.

sentences.zh: 璪字仲寶，襲瓘爵。

translations.literal: Zao, courtesy name Zhongbao, inherited Guan's noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zao, courtesy Zhongbao, inherited his father's title.

sentences.zh: 後東海王越以蘭陵益其國，改封江夏郡公，邑八千五百戶。

translations.literal: Later Prince of Donghai Yue used Lanling to augment his state; he changed enfeoffment to Duke of Jiangxia commandery, fief eight thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Yue of Donghai folded Lanling into his own domain and re-enfeoffed the house as Duke of Jiangxia with eighty-five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 懷帝即位，為散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended, he became gentleman attendant at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huai took the throne he served as gentleman attendant at leisure.

sentences.zh: 永嘉五年，沒于劉聰。

translations.literal: Yongjia year five; lost to Liu Cong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yongjia he fell captive to Liu Cong.

sentences.zh: 元帝以瓘玄孫崇嗣。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan used Guan's great-great-grandson Chong to continue succession.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan installed Wei Chong, a descendant of Wei Guan, as heir to the line.

sentences.zh: 玠字叔寶，年五歲，風神秀異。

translations.literal: Jie, courtesy name Shubao; at age five his bearing and spirit were outstanding and unusual.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jie, courtesy Shubao, was barely five when his spirit and bearing already marked him as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 祖父瓘曰：「此兒有異于眾，顧吾年老，不見其成長耳！

translations.literal: Grandfather Guan said: "This child differs from the crowd; only I am old in years; I will not see him grow to maturity!"
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wei Guan said, "This boy is unlike anyone else—yet I am old and will not live to see him grown."

sentences.zh: 」總角乘羊車入市，見者皆以為玉人，觀之者傾都。

translations.literal: " With hair bound in tufts riding a lamb cart into market; those who saw all thought him a jade man; viewers emptied the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Still a boy he rode a lamb cart through the market; onlookers mistook him for a jade statue and throngs emptied the ward to stare."

sentences.zh: 驃騎將軍王濟，玠之舅也，俊爽有風姿，每見玠，輒歎曰：「珠玉在側，覺我形穢。

translations.literal: General Who Inspires Awe Wang Ji was Jie's maternal uncle; handsome and crisp with bearing; whenever he saw Jie he always sighed saying: "Pearls and jade at my side make me feel my form foul."
translations.idiomatic: General Wang Ji—Wei Jie's uncle—was himself striking, yet whenever he saw his nephew he groaned, "With pearls and jade beside me I feel utterly coarse."

sentences.zh: 」又嘗語人曰：「與玠同遊，冏若明珠之在側，朗然照人。

translations.literal: " He also once told people saying: "Roaming with Jie is dazzling as bright pearls at one's side; brightly illuminating people."
translations.idiomatic: He told others, "Walking with Jie is like carrying luminous pearls—they light everyone nearby."

sentences.zh: 」及長，好言玄理。

translations.literal: " When grown, he loved discoursing on arcane principles.
translations.idiomatic: When he matured he loved Pure Conversation metaphysics."

sentences.zh: 其後多病體羸，母恆禁其語。

translations.literal: Afterward he often fell ill and body frail; his mother Heng forbade his speaking.
translations.idiomatic: Illness wasted him, so his mother kept forbidding him to lecture.

sentences.zh: 遇有勝日，親友時請一言，無不咨嗟，以為入微。

translations.literal: When there were fine days, relatives and friends sometimes requested one saying; none did not sigh in admiration, considering it subtle to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: On rare good days kinsmen coaxed a single sentence from him; every listener sighed that he had touched the marrow of the mystery.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王澄有高名，少所推服，每聞玠言，輒歎息絕倒。

translations.literal: Langye Wang Cheng had high fame; rarely did he defer to others; whenever he heard Jie's words he always sighed and collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng of Langye seldom praised anyone, yet each time he heard Wei Jie speak he gasped and collapsed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 故時人為之語曰：「衛玠談道，平子絕倒。

translations.literal: Therefore people of the time made a saying for him saying: "Wei Jie discourses on the Way; Pingzi collapses."
translations.idiomatic: Wits rhymed, "When Wei Jie talks doctrine, Wang Cheng topples over."

sentences.zh: 」澄及王玄、王濟並有盛名，皆出玠下，世云「王家三子，不如衛家一兒。

translations.literal: " Cheng and Wang Xuan and Wang Ji together had great fame; all ranked below Jie; the age said "The Wang clan's three sons do not match the Wei clan's one boy."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng, Wang Xuan, and Wang Ji shared glittering reputations yet stood beneath Wei Jie; folk said, "Three Wang sons cannot rival one Wei boy."

sentences.zh: 」玠妻父樂廣，有海內重名，議者以為「婦公冰清，女婿玉潤。」

translations.literal: " Jie's father-in-law Yue Guang had heavy fame within the seas; discussants considered "wife's father ice-clear; son-in-law jade-lustrous."
translations.idiomatic: Jie's father-in-law Yue Guang commanded empire-wide renown; critics called them "ice-pure father-in-law, jade-smooth son-in-law."

sentences.zh: 闢命屢至，皆不就。

translations.literal: Summons repeatedly arrived; all he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Official summons poured in; he declined every one.

sentences.zh: 久之，為太傅西閣祭酒，拜太子洗馬。

translations.literal: After a long time he became libationer of the Grand Tutor's western pavilion; appointed heir-apparent groom.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he accepted libationer at Grand Tutor Yang Jun's western pavilion, then groom to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 璪為散騎侍郎，內侍懷帝。

translations.literal: Zao was gentleman attendant at leisure; inner attendant to Emperor Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zao served Emperor Huai as gentleman attendant at leisure inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 玠以天下大亂，欲移家南行。

translations.literal: Jie because all under Heaven great chaos; wished to move family southward.
translations.idiomatic: With the realm collapsing, Wei Jie resolved to move his household south.

sentences.zh: 母曰：「我不能舍仲寶去也。

translations.literal: Mother said: "I cannot abandon Zhongbao and leave."
translations.idiomatic: His mother protested, "I cannot leave Zhongbao behind."

sentences.zh: 」玠啟諭深至，為門戶大計，母涕泣從之。

translations.literal: " Jie explained penetratingly for household great plan; mother weeping followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jie pleaded with family survival at stake until she wept and agreed."

sentences.zh: 臨別，玠謂兄曰：「在三之義，人之所重。

translations.literal: At parting Jie told elder brother saying: "The duty of the three bonds is what men esteem.
translations.idiomatic: At farewell Wei Jie told his brother, "The threefold duty binding lord, father, and teacher is everything we honor.

sentences.zh: 今可謂致身之日，兄其勉之。

translations.literal: Now can be called the day to devote body; elder brother should exert himself.
translations.idiomatic: Today is the day you devote yourself fully—brother, strive with all you have."

sentences.zh: 」乃扶輿母轉至江夏。

translations.literal: " Then supporting carriage mother shifted to Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Then he escorted his mother by litter onward to Jiangxia."

sentences.zh: 玠妻先亡。

translations.literal: Jie's wife died earlier.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jie's first wife had died.

sentences.zh: 征南將軍山簡見之，甚相欽重。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the South Shan Jian saw him; greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: General Shan Jian of the southern expedition admired him deeply.

sentences.zh: 簡曰：「昔戴叔鸞嫁女，唯賢是與，不問貴賤，況衛氏權貴門戶令望之人乎！

translations.literal: Jian said: "Formerly Dai Shuluan married daughter; only worthiness was given; not asking noble or base; how much more the Wei clan powerful noble gate command-respect person!"
translations.idiomatic: Shan said, "Long ago Dai Shuluan married his daughter solely on talent, heedless of rank—how much more so for a Wei son who heads a house of such prestige!"

sentences.zh: 」於是以女妻焉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon gave daughter as wife to him.
translations.idiomatic: He married his daughter to Wei Jie."

sentences.zh: 遂進豫章，是時大將軍王敦鎮豫章，長史謝鯤先雅重玠，相見欣然，言論彌日。

translations.literal: Then advanced to Yuzhang; at this time Grand General Wang Dun garrisoned Yuzhang; chief clerk Xie Kun earlier appreciated Jie; meeting gladly; discourse filled days.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed on to Yuzhang, where Grand General Wang Dun was stationed; Chief Clerk Xie Kun, who had long admired Wei Jie, welcomed him gladly and talked for days on end.

sentences.zh: 敦謂鯤曰：「昔王輔嗣吐金聲於中朝，此子復玉振于江表，微言之緒，絕而復續。

translations.literal: Dun told Kun saying: "Formerly Wang Fusi spat golden voice in central court; this child again jade-resonates south of the Yangzi; subtle speech's thread; broken then continued.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun told Xie Kun, "Wang Bi once rang like golden bells at Luoyang; this youth now answers like jade chimes south of the river—the thread of Pure Conversation snaps back to life."

sentences.zh: 不意永嘉之末，復聞正始之音，何平叔若在，當復絕倒。

translations.literal: I did not expect at Yongjia's end again to hear Zhengshi tones; if He Pingshu were present; would again collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Who expected, after Yongjia's ruin, to hear again the voice of Zhengshi? Were He Yan still alive he would faint away once more."

sentences.zh: 」玠嘗以人有不及，可以情恕；

translations.literal: " Jie once held that where people had inadequacy; feeling may forgive;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jie believed shortcomings deserve sympathetic forgiveness;

sentences.zh: 非意相干，可以理遣，故終身不見喜慍之容。

translations.literal: unintended offending; principle may dispatch; therefore lifelong never saw pleased-or-angry expression.
translations.idiomatic: unintended slights deserve calm reasoning—so his face never showed sudden joy or anger."

sentences.zh: 以王敦豪爽不群，而好居物上，恐非國之忠臣，求向建鄴。

translations.literal: Because Wang Dun was forthright ungrouped; yet loved occupying above others; feared not state's loyal minister; sought to go toward Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wang Dun's swagger sat ill with him—always grasping the upper hand—Wei Jie doubted he would prove a loyal servant of the state and asked leave to reach Jianye.

sentences.zh: 京師人士聞其姿容，觀者如堵。

translations.literal: Capital gentlemen hearing his bearing and appearance; viewers like a wall.
translations.idiomatic: Capital sophisticates had heard of his looks; the crowds who came to stare packed wall-tight.

sentences.zh: 玠勞疾遂甚，永嘉六年卒，時年二十七，時人謂玠被看殺。

translations.literal: Jie's exhaustion illness then extreme; Yongjia year six died; at age twenty-seven; people of the time said Jie was viewed to death.
translations.idiomatic: His fragile health collapsed under the strain; he died in the sixth year of Yongjia at twenty-seven—people said Wei Jie was literally watched to death.

sentences.zh: 葬於南昌。

translations.literal: Buried at Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: They buried him at Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 謝鯤哭之慟，人問曰：「子有何恤而致斯哀？

translations.literal: Xie Kun wept for him bitterly; people asked saying: "What sorrow do you have that brings such grief?"
translations.idiomatic: Xie Kun mourned wildly; someone asked what loss could wound him so deeply.

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「棟樑折矣，不覺哀耳。

translations.literal: " Answered saying: "The ridgepole beam is broken; unconsciously grief."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "A ridgebeam just snapped—how could I not grieve?"

sentences.zh: 」咸和中，改塋于江寧。

translations.literal: " In Xianhe era; moved tomb to Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianhe his tomb was moved to Jiangning."

sentences.zh: 丞相王導教曰：「衛洗馬明當改葬。

translations.literal: Chancellor Wang Dao instructed saying: "Wei groom tomorrow shall be moved burial.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Wang Dao ordered, "The heir-apparent groom Wei Jie will be reburied tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 此君風流名士，海內所瞻，可修薄祭，以敦舊好。

translations.literal: This lord is wind-flow famous scholar; within seas looked-to; may arrange modest sacrifice; to thicken old friendship.
translations.idiomatic: He was a paragon admired across the empire—offer a modest offering to honor old ties."

sentences.zh: 」後劉惔、謝尚共論中朝人士，或問：「杜乂可方衛洗馬不？

translations.literal: " Later Liu Tan and Xie Shang jointly discussed central court gentlemen; someone asked: "Can Du Yi match Wei groom?"
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Tan and Xie Shang ranked western Jin luminaries; someone asked whether Du Yi could compare with Groom Wei.

sentences.zh: 」尚曰：「安得相比，其間可容數人。

translations.literal: " Shang said: "How can they be compared; between them could fit several men.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shang replied, "There is no comparison—you could slip several men between them."

sentences.zh: 」惔又云：「杜乂膚清，叔寶神清。

translations.literal: " Tan further said: "Du Yi's skin clear; Shubao's spirit clear.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tan added, "Du Yi has crystalline skin; Shubao has crystalline spirit."

sentences.zh: 」其為有識者所重若此。

translations.literal: " He was by knowledgeable ones esteemed thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the regard thoughtful men paid him."

sentences.zh: 于時中興名士，唯王承及玠為當時第一云。

translations.literal: At that time restoration famous scholars; only Wang Cheng and Jie were that age's first.
translations.idiomatic: Among Restoration-era talents only Wang Cheng and Wei Jie ranked first.

sentences.zh: 恆族弟展字道舒，歷尚書郎、南陽太守。

translations.literal: Heng's clan younger cousin Zhan courtesy Daoshu; passed through secretariat gentleman, Nanyang prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Heng's kinsman Wei Zhan, courtesy Daoshu, served as secretariat gentleman and prefect of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 永嘉中，為江州刺史，累遷晉王大理。

translations.literal: In Yongjia era; became Jiangzhou inspector; accumulated promoted Jin Prince Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongjia he governed Jiangzhou and rose to minister of justice for the Jin prince.

sentences.zh: 詔有考子證父，或鞭父母問子所在，展以為恐傷正教，並奏除之。

translations.literal: Edicts had examining sons testifying fathers; or flogging parents asking where son was; Zhan considered likely harming correct teaching; jointly memorialized to abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts had forced sons to inform on fathers and even whipped parents to locate sons; Wei Zhan argued this corroded moral instruction and had both practices struck.

sentences.zh: 中興建，為廷尉，上疏宜復肉刑，語在《刑法志》。

translations.literal: Restoration established; became Minister of Justice; submitted memorial fitting restore flesh punishments; words are in 'Treatise on Punishments.'
translations.idiomatic: After the Restoration he became Minister of Justice and memorialized for restoring corporal punishment—the text sits in the Treatise on Punishments.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Died; posthumously awarded Minister of Palace Supplies.
translations.idiomatic: He died and received posthumous appointment as minister of palace supplies.

sentences.zh: 張華，字茂先，范陽方城人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua, courtesy name Maoxian, was a man of Fangcheng in Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua, courtesy Maoxian, came from Fangcheng in Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 父平，魏漁陽郡守。

translations.literal: Father Ping; Wei Yuyang commandery governor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang Ping had been governor of Yuyang under Wei.

sentences.zh: 華少孤貧，自牧羊，同郡盧欽見而器之。

translations.literal: Hua in youth was orphaned and poor; himself herded sheep; same commandery Lu Qin saw and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua was poor and fatherless, herding his own sheep, until his townsman Lu Qin spotted his promise.

sentences.zh: 鄉人劉放亦奇其才，以女妻焉。

translations.literal: Village man Liu Fang also marveled his talent; gave daughter as wife to him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang of the same district likewise prized his talent and married him to his daughter.

sentences.zh: 華學業優博，辭藻溫麗，朗贍多通，圖緯方伎之書莫不詳覽。

translations.literal: Hua's learning excellent and broad; diction warm and beautiful; clear and ample many comprehensions; chart-omen and technique books none not read in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua's learning was deep, his phrasing warm and elegant, his mind clear and encyclopedic; he pored over cosmographs, prophecies, and every technical treatise.

sentences.zh: 少自修謹，造次必以禮度。

translations.literal: Youth self cultivated cautious; in hurry-haste always by ritual measure.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he guarded his conduct; even in panic he kept ritual bounds.

sentences.zh: 勇於赴義，篤于周急。

translations.literal: Brave in pursuing righteousness; sincere in relieving urgent need.
translations.idiomatic: He rushed to justice and spent himself helping the desperate.

sentences.zh: 器識弘曠，時人罕能測之。

translations.literal: Vessel and insight vast-wide; people of the time rarely could fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: His capacity and foresight were immense—contemporaries seldom plumbed him.

sentences.zh: 初未知名，著《鷦鷯賦》以自寄。

translations.literal: At first not yet known by name; composed the 'Wren Rhapsody' to lodge himself.
translations.idiomatic: Before his name circulated he wrote the Wren Rhapsody to speak for himself.

sentences.zh: 其詞曰：

translations.literal: Its words say:
translations.idiomatic: It reads:

sentences.zh: 何造化之多端，播群形于萬類。

translations.literal: How transformation's many ends; spreading crowd forms among ten thousand kinds.
translations.idiomatic: Creation works by countless turns, scattering myriad shapes among the ten thousand things.

sentences.zh: 惟鷦鷯之微禽，亦攝生而受氣，育翩翾之陋體，無玄黃以自貴；

translations.literal: Only the wren's tiny bird; also draws life and receives qi; nurtures flutter-trilling humble body; without dark-yellow to prize itself;
translations.idiomatic: Even the tiny wren receives life and breath; its shabby fluttering frame wears no royal colors to boast with;

sentences.zh: 毛無施於器用，肉不登乎俎味。

translations.literal: fur has no application in utensils use; flesh does not ascend to chopping-board flavors.
translations.idiomatic: its feathers serve no craft and its flesh never reaches the sacrificial board.

sentences.zh: 鷹鸇過猶戢翼，尚何懼于{罒童}罻！

translations.literal: Hawks and ger-falcons passing still tuck wings; still what fear of casting-net mesh!
translations.idiomatic: Kites and goshawks bank away with folded wings—why should it dread the fowler's net?

sentences.zh: 翳薈蒙籠，是焉遊集。

translations.literal: Dense-thicket shade-cover; here roam and gather.
translations.idiomatic: It nests where scrub grows tangled and dense.

sentences.zh: 飛不飄揚，翔不翕集。

translations.literal: Flying not drifting-rise; soaring not closing-gather.
translations.idiomatic: Its flight never billows nor swoops in thundering flocks.

sentences.zh: 其居易容，其求易給；

translations.literal: Its dwelling easy accommodate; its seeking easy supply;
translations.idiomatic: Its home is easy to furnish and its needs easy to meet;

sentences.zh: 巢林不過一枝，每食不過數粒。

translations.literal: nest forest not beyond one branch; each meal not beyond several grains.
translations.idiomatic: one branch suffices for its nest; a few grains fill each meal.

sentences.zh: 棲無所滯。

translations.literal: Roosting nowhere stagnant.
translations.idiomatic: It never lingers where it roosts.

sentences.zh: 遊無所盤；

translations.literal: Roaming nowhere coil;
translations.idiomatic: It wanders without plotting a circuit;

sentences.zh: 匪陋荊棘，匪榮茝蘭。

translations.literal: Not base thorns-brambles; not glory iris-orchids.
translations.idiomatic: It neither hugs coarse brambles nor vaunts sweet orchids.

sentences.zh: 動翼而逸，投足而安。

translations.literal: Moving wings then leisurely; placing feet then peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: A flap carries it free; wherever it lights it rests secure.

sentences.zh: 委命順理，與物無患。

translations.literal: Entrust fate following pattern; with things without harm.
translations.idiomatic: It leaves fate to pattern and quarrels with nothing.

sentences.zh: 伊茲禽之無知，而處身之似智。

translations.literal: This bird's ignorance; yet placing body seems wise.
translations.idiomatic: Tiny creature without human wit, yet its conduct seems wise.

sentences.zh: 不懷寶以賈害，不飾表以招累。

translations.literal: Not cherishing treasure to trade harm; not adorning surface to invite burden.
translations.idiomatic: It hoards no glitter that buys disaster and flaunts no plumage that courts ruin.

sentences.zh: 靜守性而不矜，動因循而簡易。

translations.literal: Quietly guarding nature without pride; moving following-along and simple easy.
translations.idiomatic: Still, it keeps its nature without pride; active, it follows the simple path.

sentences.zh: 任自然以為資，無誘慕於世偽。

translations.literal: Entrust nature as resource; without lure-envy toward age falseness.
translations.idiomatic: It trusts spontaneity for sustenance and envies none of the world's sham prizes.

sentences.zh: 雕鶡介其觜距，鵠鷺軼於雲際，鶤雞竄於幽險，孔翠生乎遐裔，彼晨鳧與歸雁，又矯翼而增逝，咸美羽而豐肌，故無罪而皆斃；

translations.literal: Carving-hawks armor their beak-spurs; swans and egrets surpass cloud margins; kun-roosters dart in hidden peril; peacock-emerald born in distant borders; those morning-ducks and returning wild-geese; again straightening wings and increasing depart; all lovely feather and plump flesh; therefore without crime yet all perish;
translations.idiomatic: Armored hawks sharpen talons; swans and herons tower above the clouds; golden pheasants hide in precarious crags; kingfishers glitter on distant shores; wild ducks and migrant geese wheel skyward—all glorious plumes and meaty breasts—yet each dies guiltless;

sentences.zh: 徒銜蘆以避繳，終為戮於此世。

translations.literal: In vain holding reed to avoid spring-bolt; in end become slaughtered in this age.
translations.idiomatic: even carrying reeds to dodge bowstrings cannot save them from this slaughtering world.

sentences.zh: 蒼鷹鷙而受絏，鸚鵡慧而入籠，屈猛志以服養，塊幽縶於九重；

translations.literal: Gray goshawk fierce yet receives tether; parrot clever yet enters cage; bending fierce intent to submit nurture; lump-dark imprisoned in ninefold depths;
translations.idiomatic: Green goshawks fierce yet wear jesses; clever parrots enter cages—fierce wills bent to feed men, pent in deepest prisons;

sentences.zh: 變音聲以順旨，思摧翮而為庸。

translations.literal: Change sounds to comply intent; thinking break wings to become common.
translations.idiomatic: they twist song to suit masters and would snap their wings to stay useless pets.

sentences.zh: 戀鍾岱之林野，慕隴坻之高松。

translations.literal: Long for Zhong-Dai forests wilds; envy Longdi's high pines.
translations.idiomatic: They pine for Zhong and Tai forests and sigh for tall pines on Long Ridge.

sentences.zh: 雖蒙幸于於日，未若疇昔之從容。

translations.literal: Although receiving favor on sun; not like former-times' ease-leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Daily favor cannot match old freedom.

sentences.zh: 海鳥爰居，避風而至；

translations.literal: Sea bird Yuanju; avoiding wind then arrives;
translations.idiomatic: The seabird Yuanju fled storms to shore;

sentences.zh: 條支巨爵，逾嶺自致；

translations.literal: Tiaozhi giant finch; crossing ranges self-arrives;
translations.idiomatic: Tiaozhi's giant thrushes crossed ranges as tribute;

sentences.zh: 提挈萬里，飄颻逼畏。

translations.literal: Carried ten thousand li; drifting-wind driven fear.
translations.idiomatic: borne ten thousand li in cages, trembling with dread.

sentences.zh: 夫惟體大妨物，而形瑰足偉也。

translations.literal: Now only body large harms things; while form rare suffices greatness.
translations.idiomatic: Great bodies obstruct the world; strange shapes excite awe.

sentences.zh: 陰陽陶烝，萬品一區。

translations.literal: Yin-yang pottery-steam; ten thousand kinds one zone.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and yang forge everything in one crucible.

sentences.zh: 巨細舛錯，種繁類殊。

translations.literal: Huge-small crisscross-error; kinds numerous classes different.
translations.idiomatic: Giants and mites tangle together—species beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 鷦冥巢於蚊睫，大鵬彌乎天隅，將以上方不足而下比有餘。

translations.literal: Small-wren nests on mosquito eyelash; giant peng fills heaven corner; about to take above square insufficient and below compare surplus.
translations.idiomatic: A wren could nest on a gnat's lash while the giant roc spans heaven's edge—proof that what heaven lacks below still overflows with life.

sentences.zh: 普天壤而遐觀，吾又安知大小之所如。

translations.literal: Throughout heaven and earth I gaze far and wide; how again do I know how largeness and smallness proceed?
translations.idiomatic: I survey the breadth of heaven and earth—how am I to say what is truly great or small?

sentences.zh: 陳留阮籍見之，歎曰：「王佐之才也！

translations.literal: Chenliu Ruan Ji saw him and sighed, saying: "The talent of one who aids a king!"
translations.idiomatic: When Ruan Ji of Chenliu saw him, he sighed and said, "Here is the makings of a kingmaker!"

sentences.zh: 」由是聲名始著。

translations.literal: " From this his reputation began to be notable.
translations.idiomatic: From that moment his name began to spread.

sentences.zh: 郡守鮮于嗣薦華為太常博士。

translations.literal: The prefect Xianyu Si recommended Hua as erudite of the Chamberlain for Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Xianyu Si recommended Zhang Hua for the post of erudite of the Chamberlain for Ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 盧欽言之于文帝，轉河南尹丞，未拜，除佐著作郎。

translations.literal: Lu Qin spoke of him to Emperor Wen; he was transferred to assistant magistrate of the Henan Intendant; before receiving appointment, he was appointed assistant editorial director.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qin spoke of him to Emperor Wen; Zhang Hua was slated for assistant magistrate under the Henan Intendant but before taking office was named assistant editorial director instead.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷長史，兼中書郎。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was promoted to chief clerk and concurrently palace attendant secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he rose to chief clerk and concurrently served as palace attendant secretary.

sentences.zh: 朝議表奏，多見施用，遂即真。

translations.literal: Court deliberations and memorials were mostly seen adopted and applied; then he received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Court deliberations and memorials were largely put into practice, and he received full substantive appointment.

sentences.zh: 晉受禪，拜黃門侍郎，封關內侯。

translations.literal: When Jin received the abdication, he was appointed gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gates and enfeoffed as marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin accepted the abdication, he was made gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gates and enfeoffed as marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 華強記默識，四海之內，若指諸掌。

translations.literal: Hua had powerful memory and silent recognition; within the four seas it was as if pointing at his palm.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua's memory was prodigious—within the realm he could lay out affairs as if tracing them on his palm.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗問漢宮室制度及建章千門萬戶，華應對如流，聽者忘倦，畫地成圖，左右屬目。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once asked about Han palace regulations and Jianzhang's thousand gates and myriad doors; Hua responded as flowing water; listeners forgot weariness; he drew on the ground and formed diagrams; those left and right fixed their eyes on him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once quizzed him on Han palace layouts and Jianzhang Palace's countless gates; Zhang Hua answered without hesitation, holding his audience spellbound; he sketched plans in the dust while everyone watched rapt.

sentences.zh: 帝甚異之，時人比之子產。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly considered him unusual; people of the time compared him to Zichan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled at him; contemporaries likened him to Zichan of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 數歲，拜中書令，後加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: After several years he was appointed director of the palace secretariat; later he was additionally named regular attendant cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: A few years later he became director of the palace secretariat and was soon given the concurrent title of regular attendant cavalry.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，哀毀過禮，中詔勉勵，逼令攝事。

translations.literal: He encountered mourning for his mother; grief wasted him beyond the rites; a palace edict encouraged him and compelled him to assume duties.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he mourned so fiercely that he wasted beyond ritual bounds; an edict from the inner palace urged him on and pressed him back to office.

sentences.zh: 初，帝潛與羊祜謀伐吳，而群臣多以為不可，唯華贊成其計。

translations.literal: At first the emperor secretly with Yang Hu plotted to attack Wu, but many ministers mostly thought it not feasible; only Hua approved the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Emperor Wu had secretly planned the Wu campaign with Yang Hu, while most ministers opposed it—only Zhang Hua endorsed the strategy.

sentences.zh: 其後，祜疾篤，帝遣華詣祜，問以伐吳之計，語在《祜傳》。

translations.literal: Thereafter Hu's illness was grave; the emperor sent Hua to visit Hu and asked him concerning the plan to attack Wu; the words are in the "Hu Biography."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Yang Hu lay dying, the emperor sent Zhang Hua to consult him on the Wu campaign; the account appears in Yang Hu's biography.

sentences.zh: 及將大舉，以華為度支尚書，乃量計運漕，決定廟算。

translations.literal: When about to launch a great campaign, they made Hua Minister of Revenue; then he measured and calculated transport and canal shipping and settled the temple calculation.
translations.idiomatic: When the great offensive loomed, Zhang Hua was put in charge of revenue and logistics; he calculated supply lines and grain transport and fixed the grand strategy at court.

sentences.zh: 眾軍既進，而未有克獲，賈充等奏誅華以謝天下。

translations.literal: The mass armies had already advanced but had not yet taken victories; Jia Chong and others memorialized to execute Hua to apologize to all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The armies had marched yet scored no breakthrough; Jia Chong and others demanded Zhang Hua's execution as a gesture of atonement to the realm.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此是吾意，華但與吾同耳。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This is my intent; Hua merely was the same as I."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "This was my decision—Zhang Hua simply agreed with me."

sentences.zh: 」時大臣皆以為未可輕進，華獨堅執，以為必克。

translations.literal: " At the time great ministers all thought one must not lightly advance; Hua alone firmly held and thought there would certainly be conquest.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile senior ministers argued against rushing the advance; Zhang Hua alone held fast that Wu would fall.

sentences.zh: 及吳滅，詔曰：「尚書、關內侯張華，前與故太傅羊祜共創大計，遂典掌軍事，部分諸方，算定權略，運籌決勝，有謀謨之勳。

translations.literal: When Wu was destroyed, an edict said: "Minister, Marquis within the Passes Zhang Hua, formerly with the late Grand Tutor Yang Hu together created the great plan; then he oversaw military affairs, deployed various regions, calculated and settled strategies and plans, planned at the command tent and determined victory; he has the merit of counsel and planning.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu fell, an edict declared: "Minister Zhang Hua, Marquis within the Passes, once joined the late Grand Tutor Yang Hu in devising the grand design; he then directed military affairs, coordinated the fronts, weighed strategy, and planned victory at headquarters—meritorious counsel indeed."

sentences.zh: 其進封為廣武縣侯，增邑萬戶，封子一人為亭侯，千五百戶，賜絹萬匹。」

translations.literal: Advance him to be enfeoffed as marquis of Guangwu County; increase fief by ten thousand households; enfeoff one son as village marquis, fifteen hundred households; grant ten thousand bolts of silk."
translations.idiomatic: Promote him to Marquis of Guangwu County, add ten thousand households to his fief, enfeoff one son as village marquis with fifteen hundred households, and grant ten thousand bolts of silk."

sentences.zh: 華名重一世，眾所推服，晉史及儀禮憲章並屬於華，多所損益。

translations.literal: Hua's name weighed on one generation; all deferred to him; Jin histories and ritual statutes and regulations together belonged to Hua; there were many reductions and additions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua's stature dominated his age; everyone deferred to him. The Jin court histories and ritual codes alike passed through his hands, with countless revisions.

sentences.zh: 當時詔誥皆所草定，聲譽益盛，有台輔之望焉。

translations.literal: At the time edicts and pronouncements were all drafted by him; reputation grew ever greater; there was the expectation of terrace minister.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial edicts of the day were drafted in his hand; his fame swelled until men looked to him as a future chief minister.

sentences.zh: 而荀勖自以大族，恃帝恩深，憎疾之，每伺間隙，欲出華外鎮。

translations.literal: But Xun Xu considered himself a great clan and relied on the emperor's favor being deep; he hated him; each time he watched for openings and wished to send Hua out to an outer command.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xun Xu, swaggering as scion of a great house and secure in imperial favor, loathed Zhang Hua and watched for every chance to post him away from the capital.

sentences.zh: 會帝問華：「誰可託寄後事者？

translations.literal: It happened the emperor asked Hua: "Who may be entrusted with affairs after death?"
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Wu asked Zhang Hua, "Whom can I trust with what comes after me?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「明德至親，莫如齊王攸。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Of clarifying virtue and utmost kinship, none matches Prince of Qi You."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Among those of shining virtue and closest blood, none rivals Prince Sima You of Qi."

sentences.zh: 」既非上意所在，微為忤旨，間言遂行。

translations.literal: " It was not where the superior's intent lay; slightly he offended the decree; slanderous words then proceeded.
translations.idiomatic: That was not what the emperor wished to hear—a subtle breach of imperial intent—and calumny soon found its opening.

sentences.zh: 乃出華為持節、都督幽州諸軍事、領護烏桓校尉、安北將軍。

translations.literal: Then they sent out Hua as credential-bearing, supervisor of military affairs of Youzhou and all related matters, concurrently colonel-protector of the Wuhuan, general who pacifies the north.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua was therefore posted as commander of Youzhou with imperial insignia, concurrently colonel-protector of the Wuhuan and general who pacifies the north.

sentences.zh: 撫納新舊，戎夏懷之。

translations.literal: He soothed and received new and old; Rong and Xia cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: He won over old allies and new subjects alike; barbarian and Han peoples alike embraced him.

sentences.zh: 東夷馬韓、新彌諸國依山帶海，去州四千餘里，歷世未附者二十餘國，並遣使朝獻。

translations.literal: Eastern Yi Mahan, Xinmi and various states leaned on mountains and belted the sea; distant from the province more than four thousand li; through generations not submitting were more than twenty states; together they sent envoys to court to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The Mahan and Xinmi peoples of the eastern Yi, coastal and mountainous, lay over four thousand li from the province; more than twenty lands that had never submitted through the ages now sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 於是遠夷賓服，四境無虞，頻歲豐稔，士馬強盛。

translations.literal: Thereupon distant Yi submitted as guests; the four borders had no anxiety; successive years were abundant harvests; soldiers and horses were strong and flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: The distant tribes submitted; the frontiers stayed quiet; harvests ran rich year after year; troops and mounts grew formidable.

sentences.zh: 朝議欲徵華入相，又欲進號儀同。

translations.literal: Court deliberation wished to summon Hua to enter as minister and also wished to advance his title to ceremony equal.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated recalling Zhang Hua as chief minister and advancing his rank to ceremony equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 初，華毀徵士馮恢於帝，紞即恢之弟也，深有寵於帝。

translations.literal: At first Hua slandered summoned scholar Feng Hui before the emperor; Dan was Hui's younger brother and deeply had favor from the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhang Hua had maligned the summoned scholar Feng Hui to the throne; Feng Dan was Feng Hui's younger brother and stood high in imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 紞嘗侍帝，從容論魏晉事，因曰；

translations.literal: Dan once attended the emperor; calmly discussed Wei and Jin affairs; then said;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dan once attended the emperor and, speaking calmly of Wei and Jin history, went on to say:

sentences.zh: 「臣竊謂鍾會之釁，頗由太祖。

translations.literal: "Your servant privately considers Zhong Hui's calamity largely derived from Emperor Taizu."
translations.idiomatic: "Your servant ventures that Zhong Hui's rebellion owed much to Emperor Taizu of Wei."

sentences.zh: 」帝變色曰：「卿何言邪！

translations.literal: " The emperor changed color and said: "What words do you speak!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face darkened. "What are you saying?"

sentences.zh: 」紞免冠謝曰；

translations.literal: " Dan removed cap and apologized, saying;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dan doffed his cap and apologized:

sentences.zh: 「臣愚冗瞽言，罪應萬死。

translations.literal: "Your servant foolish redundant blind speech; guilt deserves ten thousand deaths."
translations.idiomatic: "Your servant spoke rash nonsense and deserves death ten thousand times over."

sentences.zh: 然臣微意，猶有可申。

translations.literal: Yet your servant's subtle intent still has what may be extended.
translations.idiomatic: Yet there is still a thread of meaning your servant may unfold.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「何以言之」紞曰：「臣以為善禦者必識六轡盈縮之勢，善政者必審官方控帶之宜，故仲由以兼人被抑，冉求以退弱被進，漢高八王以寵過夷滅，光武諸將由抑損克終。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "How do you say it?" Dan said: "Your servant considers that one good at controlling horses must recognize the six reins' expansion and contraction momentum; one good at governance must examine official patterns and belt-control suitability; therefore Zhong You was suppressed for being able in many things; Ran Qiu was advanced for retreat and weakness; Han Gao's eight kings through excessive favor were extinguished; Guangwu's various generals through restraint and reduction achieved their end.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked how he meant it. Feng Dan replied: "A skilled charioteer reads slack and taut in the reins; a wise ruler gauges how offices balance power. Hence Zhong You was checked for being too capable, Ran Qiu promoted for seeming modest; Liu Bang's princes were ruined by indulgence, Guangwu's generals survived because he kept them humble."

sentences.zh: 非上有仁暴之殊，下有愚智之異，蓋抑揚與奪使之然耳。

translations.literal: It is not that above there is benevolence and cruelty difference, below foolishness and wisdom difference; cover suppression and elevation and granting and seizing made it thus.
translations.idiomatic: It was not a matter of benevolent versus cruel rulers or foolish versus wise subjects—promotion, demotion, reward, and seizure shaped the outcome.

sentences.zh: 鍾會才見有限，而太祖誇獎太過，嘉其謀猷，盛其名器，居以重勢，委以大兵，故使會自謂算無遺策，功在不賞，輈張跋扈，遂構凶逆耳。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui's talent insight was limited, yet Emperor Taizu praised and rewarded excessively; praised his planning strategies; magnified his name and vessels; situated him with heavy power; entrusted him with great armies; therefore caused Hui himself to consider calculations left no strategy out; merit lay beyond reward; arrogant and domineering; then structured fierce rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui's gifts were modest, yet Emperor Taizu flattered him, praised his schemes, heaped titles on him, seated him in vast authority, and handed him whole armies—until Zhong Hui believed his plans infallible and his deeds beyond reward; he swelled with arrogance and turned traitor.

sentences.zh: 向令太祖錄其小能，節以大禮，抑之以權勢，納之以軌則，則亂心無由而生，亂事無由而成矣。

translations.literal: Had ordered Emperor Taizu record his small abilities, restrain with great rites, suppress him with power and momentum, accept him with tracks and rules, then chaotic heart had no cause to arise, chaotic affairs had no cause to complete.
translations.idiomatic: Had Taizu acknowledged only Zhong Hui's modest talents, curbed him with ritual, checked him with authority, and bound him with rules, neither rebellious intent nor rebellion itself could have taken shape.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「然。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "So."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "So it is."

sentences.zh: 」紞稽首曰：「陛下既已然微臣之言，宜思堅冰之漸，無使如會之徒復致覆喪。

translations.literal: " Dan knocked head and said: "Your Majesty having already approved your petty servant's words, ought consider hard ice's gradual advance; do not cause such as Hui's kind again to bring overturn and loss.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dan kowtowed. "Since Your Majesty accepts your servant's words, ponder how thick ice forms drop by drop—do not let another Zhong Hui bring ruin again."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「當今豈有如會者乎？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Present age how could there be such as Hui?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Is there anyone today like Zhong Hui?"

sentences.zh: 」紞曰：「東方朔有言『談何容易』，《易》曰：『臣不密則失身』。

translations.literal: " Dan said: "Dongfang Shuo had words 'speaking how easy'; the Changes says: 'When ministers are not secret then lose body.'"
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dan answered, "Dongfang Shuo warned that speaking out is no simple matter; the Book of Changes says, 'If a minister is not discreet, he loses his life.'"

sentences.zh: 」帝乃屏左右曰：「卿極言之。

translations.literal: " The emperor then screened left and right and said: "You exhaustively speak it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed his attendants. "Speak plainly."

sentences.zh: 」紞曰：「陛下謀謨之臣，著大功於天下，海內莫不聞知，據方鎮總戎馬之任者，皆在陛下聖慮矣。

translations.literal: " Dan said: "Your Majesty's counsel-planning ministers who established great merit under heaven; within the seas none do not hear and know; those who hold regional commands and overall horse-of-war duties are all within Your Majesty's sagely consideration.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dan said, "Your counselors who shaped the realm's greatest deeds are known to every corner of the empire—those who command the provinces and armies already weigh on Your Majesty's mind."

sentences.zh: 」帝默然。

translations.literal: " The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent.

sentences.zh: 頃之，徵華為太常。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Hua was summoned as Chamberlain for Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zhang Hua was recalled as Chamberlain for Ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 以太廟屋棟折，免官。

translations.literal: Because the Grand Temple rafters broke, he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When a roof beam of the Grand Ancestral Temple snapped, he lost his post.

sentences.zh: 遂終帝之世，以列侯朝見。

translations.literal: Then to the end of the emperor's generation, as full marquis he attended court audience.
translations.idiomatic: For the rest of Emperor Wu's reign he attended court only as a full marquis.

sentences.zh: 惠帝即位，以華為太子少傅，與王戎、裴楷、和嶠俱以德望為楊駿所忌，皆不與朝政。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui ascended the throne, they made Hua junior tutor to the crown prince; together with Wang Rong, Pei Kai, He Jiao, all because of virtue reputation were envied by Yang Jun; none participated in court governance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui named Zhang Hua junior tutor to the heir apparent; together with Wang Rong, Pei Kai, and He Jiao—men whose reputations drew Yang Jun's jealousy—they were shut out of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 及駿誅後，將廢皇太后，會群臣於朝堂，議者皆承望風旨，以為《春秋》絕文姜，今太后自絕于宗廟，亦宜廢黜。

translations.literal: When after Jun was executed they were about to depose the empress dowager; they assembled many ministers at the court hall; debaters all carried expectation of wind decree; thought the Spring and Autumn cuts off Wen Jiang; now empress dowager herself cut off from ancestral temples; also ought be deposed.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Jun fell, ministers gathered in the hall to strip the empress dowager of title; eager to read the emperor's mood, they cited how the Spring and Autumn Annals severed ties with Wen Jiang—the dowager, they said, had cast off the ancestral temples and likewise deserved deposition.

sentences.zh: 」惟華議以為「夫婦之道，父不能得之於子，子不能得之于父，皇太后非得罪于先帝者也。

translations.literal: " Only Hua debated considering "the way of husband and wife; father cannot obtain it in son; son cannot obtain it in father; empress dowager is not one who offended the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhang Hua argued that "between husband and wife, neither parent nor child may dictate the bond—the empress dowager committed no offense against the late emperor."

sentences.zh: 今黨其所親，為不母於聖世，宜依漢廢趙太后為孝成后故事，貶太后之號，還稱武皇后，居異宮，以全貴終之恩」。

translations.literal: Now factioning those she is kin to; acting unmotherly in a sage age; ought follow Han's deposing Empress Zhao Zhao as Empress Dowager Xiaocheng precedent; demote empress dowager's title; return to being called Empress Wu; dwell in different palace; thereby complete the grace of honorable end."
translations.idiomatic: She favored her own clan and failed as a mother in this enlightened age; follow the Han precedent that reduced Empress Zhao to Empress Dowager Xiaocheng—strip her dowager title, restore her as Empress Wu, house her apart, and grant her a dignified death."

sentences.zh: 不從，遂廢太后為庶人。

translations.literal: They did not follow; then deposed empress dowager as common person.
translations.idiomatic: The court rejected his plea and reduced the empress dowager to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 楚王瑋受密詔殺太宰汝南王亮、太保衛瓘等，內外兵擾，朝廷大恐，計無所出。

translations.literal: Prince of Chu Wei received secret edict killing grand steward Prince of Runan Liang, grand protector Wei Guan and others; inner and outer troops disturbed; court greatly feared; plans had none to issue.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Wei of Chu, acting on a secret edict, slew Grand Steward Prince Sima Liang of Runan, Grand Guardian Wei Guan, and others; armies rioted inside and outside the palace; the court panicked and could find no policy.

sentences.zh: 華白帝以「瑋矯詔擅害二公，將士倉卒，謂是國家意，故從之耳。

translations.literal: Hua informed the emperor that "Wei forged edict and on his own harmed the two dukes; officers and soldiers hastily thought it was state's intent; therefore followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua told the emperor that Wei had forged the edict and murdered the two dukes on his own authority; troops had obeyed in haste, believing it imperial policy.

sentences.zh: 今可遣騶虞幡使外軍解嚴，理必風靡。

translations.literal: Now may dispatch zouyu banner causing outer armies to lift alert; principle certainly wind-scatters.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatch the zouyu banner to stand down the outer armies—they will scatter like wind before it.

sentences.zh: 」上從之，瑋兵果敗。

translations.literal: " The superior followed it; Wei's troops indeed were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and Wei's forces collapsed.

sentences.zh: 及瑋誅，華以首謀有功，拜右光祿大夫、開府儀同三司、侍中、中書監，金章紫綬。

translations.literal: When Wei was executed, Hua because first-planning had merit was appointed senior household grandee of the right, general-in-chief opening office ceremony equal three dukes, palace attendant, director of palace secretariat supervision, golden seal purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei's execution Zhang Hua was credited with the decisive counsel and named senior household grandee of the right, general-in-chief with ceremony equal to the Three Dukes, palace attendant, and director of the palace secretariat, with golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 固辭開府。

translations.literal: He firmly declined opening office.
translations.idiomatic: He steadfastly declined the general-in-chief opening-office privilege.

sentences.zh: 賈謐與后共謀，以華庶族，儒雅有籌略，進無逼上之嫌，退為眾望所依，欲倚以朝綱，訪以政事。

translations.literal: Jia Mi and empress together plotted; considering Hua common clan, scholarly elegant having strategy and planning; advancing without forcing superior suspicion; retreating as multitude expectation relies on; wished to lean on him for court principle; inquire him on governance affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mi and Empress Jia conspired to lean on Zhang Hua—a man of humble pedigree yet scholarly polish and strategic sense who posed no threat to the throne yet commanded universal respect—as the backbone of government and advisor on policy.

sentences.zh: 疑而未決，以問裴頠，頠素重華，深贊其事。

translations.literal: Doubted and not yet decided; asked Pei Wei; Wei always esteemed Hua; deeply praised the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Still hesitant, they consulted Pei Wei, who had long revered Zhang Hua and urged the plan wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 華遂盡忠匡輔，彌縫補闕，雖當暗主虐後之朝，而海內晏然，華之功也。

translations.literal: Hua then exhausted loyalty aiding and assisting; stitched and mended filling gaps; although facing dark lord cruel empress court; yet within seas tranquil; Hua's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua served with utter loyalty, patching every breach; even under a dim sovereign and vicious empress the realm stayed calm—credit belongs to him.

sentences.zh: 華懼后族之盛，作《女史箴》以為諷。

translations.literal: Hua feared empress clan's flourishing; composed "Female Scribe Admonitions" to serve as indirect criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Wary of the empress's clan, Zhang Hua wrote "Admonitions for the Palace Women" as veiled counsel.

sentences.zh: 賈后雖凶妒，而知敬重華。

translations.literal: Empress Jia although fierce jealous; yet knew respect revere Hua.
translations.idiomatic: For all her cruelty and jealousy, Empress Jia still respected Zhang Hua.

sentences.zh: 久之，論前後忠勳，進封壯武郡公。

translations.literal: After long time, debating front and rear loyal merit; advanced enfeoffment as duke of Zhuangwu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After weighing his loyal service past and present, the court promoted him to Duke of Zhuangwu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 華十餘讓，中詔敦譬，乃受。

translations.literal: Hua declined more than ten times; palace edict earnestly exhorted; then accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua declined more than ten times until inner-court edicts pressed him to yield.

sentences.zh: 數年，代下邳王晃為司空，領著作。

translations.literal: Several years, succeeded Prince of Xiapi Huang as minister of works; concurrently directed composition.
translations.idiomatic: A few years later he succeeded Prince Sima Huang of Xiapi as minister of works while directing the historiography office.

sentences.zh: 及賈后謀廢太子，左衛率劉卞甚為太子所信遇，每會宴，卞必預焉。

translations.literal: When Empress Jia plotted to depose crown prince; left guard commander Liu Bian greatly was trusted and favored by crown prince; each time gathering banquet; Bian necessarily participated therein.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Jia plotted to remove the heir apparent, Liu Bian, commander of the left guard and a man the heir deeply trusted, attended every banquet.

sentences.zh: 屢見賈謐驕傲，太子恨之，形於言色，謐亦不能平。

translations.literal: Repeatedly saw Jia Mi arrogant; crown prince hated him; formed in words and expression; Mi also could not be placid.
translations.idiomatic: Time and again he watched Jia Mi's arrogance fuel the heir's resentment, plain on the prince's face, while Mi simmered with his own grievance.

sentences.zh: 卞以賈后謀問華，華曰：「不聞。

translations.literal: Bian with Empress Jia's plot asked Hua; Hua said: "Have not heard.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bian asked Zhang Hua about the empress's plot; Zhang Hua replied, "I have heard nothing."

sentences.zh: 」卞曰：「卞以寒悴，自須昌小吏受公成拔，以至今日。

translations.literal: " Bian said: "Bian because cold destitute; from Xuchang petty clerk received lord's completion elevation; reaching today.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bian said, "I rose from a cold-handed clerk in Xuchang through your patronage to where I stand today."

sentences.zh: 士感知己，是以盡言，而公更有疑于卞邪！

translations.literal: Gentleman feels knowing-self; therefore exhaust speech; yet lord additionally has doubt toward Bian!
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman repays one who knows him—I speak plainly—yet you still mistrust me?"

sentences.zh: 」華曰：「假令有此，君欲如何？

translations.literal: " Hua said: "Suppose there be this; lord wishes how?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua asked, "Suppose it were true—what would you do?"

sentences.zh: 」卞曰：「東宮俊乂如林，四率精兵萬人。

translations.literal: " Bian said: "Eastern palace worthy talents like forest; four rates elite troops ten thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bian answered, "The heir's residence teems with talent; the four guard commands field ten thousand crack troops."

sentences.zh: 公居阿衡之任，若得公命，皇太子因朝入錄尚書事，廢賈后於金墉城，兩黃門力耳。

translations.literal: Lord occupies Yi-Yin's duty; if obtain lord's command; imperial crown prince thereby at court enters recording Masters of Writing affairs; depose Empress Jia at Metal-Walled Fortress city; two yellow gates strength ear.
translations.idiomatic: You stand as chief minister—give the word and the heir can enter court to oversee the Masters of Writing, lock Empress Jia in Jinyong Fortress; two palace attendants could manage it."

sentences.zh: 」華曰：「今天子當陽，太子，人子也，吾又不受阿衡之命，忽相與行此，是無其君父，而以不孝示天下也。

translations.literal: " Hua said: "Now Son of Heaven faces yang; crown prince is person's son; I moreover do not receive Yi-Yin's command; suddenly mutual doing this; this is without its lord father; and thereby unfilial display to all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua replied, "The emperor holds the sun throne; the heir is a son like any other; I hold no Yi Yin mandate—move rashly and we abandon sovereign and father alike and proclaim our unfilial shame to the world."

sentences.zh: 雖能有成，猶不免罪，況權戚滿朝，威柄不一，而可以安乎！

translations.literal: Although able have success; still not avoid guilt; moreover powerful kin fill court; authority handles not one; yet can be secure!
translations.idiomatic: Even success would leave guilt on our heads—how much less when powerful in-laws choke the court and authority splinters everywhere?"

sentences.zh: 」及帝會群臣於式乾殿，出太子手書，遍示群臣，莫敢有言者。

translations.literal: " When emperor assembled many ministers at Shi-Qian Hall; produced crown prince hand writing; everywhere showed many ministers; none dared have speakers.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui gathered his ministers at Shiqiang Hall and produced the heir's handwriting for all to see, none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 惟華諫曰；

translations.literal: Only Hua remonstrated saying;
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhang Hua objected:

sentences.zh: 「此國之大禍。

translations.literal: "This state's great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: "This court courts catastrophe."

sentences.zh: 自漢武以來，每廢黜正嫡，恆至喪亂。

translations.literal: From Han Wu onward, each time deposing legitimate heir; always arrived at loss and chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Wu of Han, every deposition of the legitimate heir has ended in ruin.

sentences.zh: 且國家有天下日淺，願陛下詳之。

translations.literal: Moreover state possesses all under heaven days shallow; wish Your Majesty examine it.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's grip on the realm is still fresh—think carefully, Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」尚書左僕射裴頠以為宜先檢校傳書者，又請比校太子手書，不然，恐有詐妄。

translations.literal: " Minister of Works left vice-director Pei Wei thought ought first inspect letter-carriers; also requested compare crown prince hand writing; if not; feared there would be fraud falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Wei, left vice-director of the Masters of Writing, urged them first to question whoever carried the letters and to compare them with the heir's genuine script—otherwise forgery might slip through.

sentences.zh: 賈后乃內出太子素啟事十餘紙，眾人比視，亦無敢言非者，議至日西不決，后知華等意堅，因表乞免為庶人，帝乃可其奏。

translations.literal: Empress Jia then inner produced crown prince plain memorial affairs more than ten sheets; multitude compared viewing; also none dared speak wrong ones; deliberation reached sun west undecided; empress knew Hua and others intent firm; thereby memorial begged removal as common person; emperor then approved her memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia produced more than ten pages of the heir's routine memorials from the women's quarters; no one dared call them false. Debate dragged until sunset without resolution. Seeing Zhang Hua's resolve, the empress memorialized to reduce the heir to commoner status, and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 初，趙王倫為鎮西將軍，撓亂關中，氐羌反叛，乃以梁王肜代之。

translations.literal: At first Prince of Zhao Lun was general who guards the west; disturbed Guanzhong; Di and Qiang rebelled; then with Prince of Liang Tong replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Prince Sima Lun of Zhao had served as general who guards the west and thrown Guanzhong into turmoil until the Di and Qiang rose; Prince Sima Tong of Liang replaced him.

sentences.zh: 或說華曰：「趙王貪昧，信用孫秀，所在為亂，而秀變詐，奸人之雄。

translations.literal: Someone persuaded Hua saying: "Prince of Zhao greedy dark; trusts employs Sun Xiu; wherever is chaos; yet Xiu changes deceit; villain people's champion.
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged Zhang Hua: "Prince Lun is grasping and trusts Sun Xiu, who sows chaos wherever he goes—a slippery schemer among villains."

sentences.zh: 今可遣梁王斬秀，刈趙之半，以謝關右，不亦可乎！

translations.literal: Now may dispatch Prince of Liang behead Xiu; reap Zhao's half; thereby apologize to Guan right; is it not also acceptable!
translations.idiomatic: Send Prince Tong to execute Xiu, cripple Lun's faction, and appease the western marches—why not?"

sentences.zh: 」華從之，肜許諾。

translations.literal: " Hua followed it; Tong promised.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua agreed, and Tong promised.

sentences.zh: 秀友人辛冉從西來，言於肜曰：「氐羌自反，非秀之為。

translations.literal: Xiu's friend Xin Ran from west came; spoke to Tong saying: "Di and Qiang themselves rebelled; not Xiu's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu's friend Xin Ran arrived from the west and told Tong the Di and Qiang had risen on their own—not Xiu's plot.

sentences.zh: 」故得免死。

translations.literal: " Therefore obtained exempt death.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Xiu escaped execution.

sentences.zh: 倫既還，諂事賈后，因求錄尚書事，後又求尚書令。

translations.literal: Lun having returned; flattered serving Empress Jia; thereby sought recording Masters of Writing affairs; afterward again sought director of Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: After Lun returned he curried favor with Empress Jia, demanding oversight of the Masters of Writing and later the director's seat.

sentences.zh: 華與裴頠皆固執不可，由是致怨，倫、秀疾華如仇。

translations.literal: Hua and Pei Wei both firmly held not permissible; thereby incurred resentment; Lun, Xiu hated Hua like enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua and Pei Wei blocked him both times; Lun and Sun Xiu came to hate Zhang Hua as a mortal foe.

sentences.zh: 武庫火，華懼因此變作，列兵固守，然後救之，故累代之寶及漢高斬蛇劍、王莽頭、孔子屐等盡焚焉。

translations.literal: Armory fire; Hua feared thereby change arise; arrayed troops firmly guarded; then rescued it; therefore successive generations' treasures and Han Gao's snake-slaying sword, Wang Mang's head, Confucius's sandals and others entirely burned.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial armory caught fire Zhang Hua feared a coup; he ringed it with troops before fighting the blaze, so treasures of many dynasties—including Liu Bang's snake sword, Wang Mang's pickled head, and Confucius's wooden shoes—burned away.

sentences.zh: 時華見劍穿屋而飛，莫知所向。

translations.literal: At the time Hua saw sword pierce roof and fly; none knew where it went.
translations.idiomatic: Witnesses swore they saw a sword burst through the roof and fly off—none knew where it landed.

sentences.zh: 初，華所封壯武郡有桑化為柏，識者以為不詳。

translations.literal: At first Hua's enfeoffed Zhuangwu commandery had mulberry transform into cypress; knowledgeable ones considered it not auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Zhang Hua's Zhuangwu fief mulberries turned to cypress—those versed in omens called it ill-starred.

sentences.zh: 又華第舍及監省數有妖怪。

translations.literal: Also Hua's mansion residences and supervisor bureau repeatedly had demon anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: Strange apparitions kept plaguing Zhang Hua's residence and his ministry offices.

sentences.zh: 少子韙以中台星坼，勸華遜位。

translations.literal: Younger son Wei because central terrace star split, urged Hua yield position.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Zhang Wei, citing the split of the Central Terrace star, urged him to resign.

sentences.zh: 華不從，曰；

translations.literal: Hua did not follow; said;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua refused and said:

sentences.zh: 「天道玄遠，惟修德以應之耳。

translations.literal: "Heaven's way is profound distant; only cultivate virtue thereby respond to it."
translations.idiomatic: "Heaven's purposes lie beyond our grasp—we answer them only by cultivating virtue."

sentences.zh: 不如靜以待之，以俟天命。

translations.literal: Better quietly await it; thereby await heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Better stay calm and wait out heaven's decree."

sentences.zh: 」及倫、秀將廢賈后，秀使司馬雅夜告華曰：「今社稷將危，趙王欲與公共匡朝廷，為霸者之事。

translations.literal: " When Lun and Xiu were about to depose Empress Jia, Xiu sent Sima Ya by night to tell Hua saying: "Now altars of soil and grain will be endangered; Prince of Zhao wishes with lord together rectify court; do hegemon's affair.
translations.idiomatic: When Lun and Sun Xiu prepared to depose Empress Jia, Xiu sent Sima Ya by night to Zhang Hua: "The altars are tottering; Prince Zhao wishes to join you in restoring the court and acting as the strongman who sets things right."

sentences.zh: 」華知秀等必成篡奪，乃距之。

translations.literal: " Hua knew Xiu and others would surely accomplish usurpation-seizure; then refused him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua knew Xiu meant usurpation and turned him down cold."

sentences.zh: 雅怒曰：「刃將加頸，而吐言如此！

translations.literal: Ya angrily said: "Blade about to add neck; yet spit words thus!"
translations.idiomatic: Ya snapped, "The blade is at your throat—yet this is what you say!"

sentences.zh: 」不顧而出。

translations.literal: " Without looking back exited.
translations.idiomatic: He stalked out without a backward glance."

sentences.zh: 華方晝臥，忽夢見屋壞，覺而惡之。

translations.literal: Hua was just daytime lying; suddenly dreamed seeing house ruined; awoke and loathed it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua was napping at midday when he dreamed his roof collapsed; he woke with foreboding.

sentences.zh: 是夜難作，詐稱詔召華，遂與裴頠俱被收。

translations.literal: That night disaster arose; falsely claimed edict summoned Hua; then together with Pei Wei both were seized.
translations.idiomatic: That night the coup struck; forged edicts summoned Zhang Hua, and he and Pei Wei were arrested together.

sentences.zh: 華將死，謂張林曰：「卿欲害忠臣耶？

translations.literal: Hua about to die, said to Zhang Lin: "Do you wish harm loyal minister?"
translations.idiomatic: As death closed in Zhang Hua asked Zhang Lin, "Do you mean to murder a loyal servant of the throne?"

sentences.zh: 」林稱詔詰曰：「卿為宰相，任天下事，太子之廢，不能死節，何也」華曰：「式乾之議，臣諫事具存，非不諫也。

translations.literal: " Lin claimed edict interrogated saying: "You as chief minister, shoulder all-under-heaven affairs; crown prince's deposition; could not die for integrity; why?" Hua said: "Shi-Qian hall's deliberation; subject remonstrance matters completely exist; was not not remonstrating.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lin brandished an edict and demanded: "You were chief minister charged with the realm—why did you not die for principle when the heir was cast aside?" Zhang Hua answered, "Every word I spoke against it at Shiqiang Hall is on record—I did remonstrate."

sentences.zh: 」林曰：「諫若不從，何不去位？

translations.literal: " Lin said: "If remonstrance not followed; why not leave position?"
translations.idiomatic: Lin shot back, "If they ignored your counsel, why did you not resign?"

sentences.zh: 」華不能答。

translations.literal: " Hua could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua had no reply."

sentences.zh: 須臾，使者至曰：「詔斬公。

translations.literal: Shortly, envoy arrived saying: "Edict beheads lord."
translations.idiomatic: Moments later a messenger arrived: "The edict orders your execution."

sentences.zh: 」華曰：「臣先帝老臣，中心如丹。

translations.literal: " Hua said: "Subject late emperor's old minister; center heart like cinnabar."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua said, "I am an old servant of the late emperor; my heart burns red as cinnabar."

sentences.zh: 臣不愛死，懼王室之難，禍不可測也。

translations.literal: Subject does not cherish death; fears royal house's calamity; disaster cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: I do not cling to life—I fear what calamities may yet strike the royal house."

sentences.zh: 」遂害之于前殿馬道南，夷三族，朝野莫不悲痛之。

translations.literal: " Then harmed him at front hall horse-road south; extirpated three clans; court and wild none did not grieve him.
translations.idiomatic: They cut him down south of the carriage lane before the front hall and wiped out three generations of his kin; court and countryside mourned."

sentences.zh: 時年六十九。

translations.literal: At the time age sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 華性好人物，誘進不倦，至於窮賤候門之士有一介之善者，便咨嗟稱詠，為之延譽。

translations.literal: Hua's nature loved persons; enticing advancing untiring; reaching poor low gate-waiting gentlemen having one scrap goodness; then sigh praise chant; for them extend fame.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua delighted in nurturing talent and never tired of lifting others; even a penniless scholar waiting at his gate who showed the slightest merit drew his praise and public endorsement.

sentences.zh: 雅愛書籍，身死之日，家無餘財，惟有文史溢於機篋。

translations.literal: Elegantly loved books; body death day; house had no surplus wealth; only literary histories overflowed chests.
translations.idiomatic: He adored books; when he died his house held no spare coin—only histories and belles-lettres bursting from his trunks.

sentences.zh: 嘗徙居，載書三十乘。

translations.literal: Once moved residence; loaded books thirty carts.
translations.idiomatic: When he moved house once, thirty cartloads carried nothing but books.

sentences.zh: 秘書監摯虞撰定官書，皆資華之本以取正焉。

translations.literal: Chamberlain of Palace Library Zhi Yu compiled settled official books; all relied on Hua's texts to take correctness.
translations.idiomatic: When Director Zhi Yu of the Palace Library collated the official canon, he used Zhang Hua's editions as the authoritative text.

sentences.zh: 天下奇秘，世所稀有者，悉在華所。

translations.literal: Under heaven strange secret; age rare had; all were at Hua's place.
translations.idiomatic: Every rare curiosity in the realm seemed to end up in Zhang Hua's library.

sentences.zh: 由是博物洽聞，世無與比。

translations.literal: From this broadly investigate extensive hearing; age none with compare.
translations.idiomatic: Hence his erudition was unmatched in his time.

sentences.zh: 惠帝中，人有得鳥毛三丈，以示華。

translations.literal: Mid Emperor Hui, someone obtained bird feather three zhang; to show Hua.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Hui's reign someone brought Zhang Hua a bird feather thrice ten feet long.

sentences.zh: 華見，慘然曰：「此謂海鳧毛也，出則天下亂矣。

translations.literal: Hua saw; mournfully said: "This is called sea mallard feather; when appears then all under heaven chaotic."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua turned pale. "That is the feather of the sea drake—when it appears the realm falls into chaos."

sentences.zh: 」陸機嘗餉華鮓，于時賓客滿座，華發器，便曰：「此龍肉也。

translations.literal: " Lu Ji once presented Hua pickled fish; at the time guests filled seats; Hua opened vessel; then said: "This is dragon meat.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji once sent Zhang Hua cured fish; when guests packed the hall Zhang Hua lifted the lid and declared, "This is dragon flesh."

sentences.zh: 」眾未之信，華曰：「試以苦酒濯之，必有異。

translations.literal: " Multitude not yet believed it; Hua said: "Try with bitter wine wash it; necessarily has strangeness.
translations.idiomatic: No one believed him until Zhang Hua said, "Rinse it in vinegar—something strange will happen."

sentences.zh: 」既而五色光起。

translations.literal: " Thenafter five-color light arose.
translations.idiomatic: A moment later five-colored light flared up."

sentences.zh: 機還問鮓主，果云：「園中茅積下得一白魚，質狀殊常，以作鮓，過美，故以相獻。

translations.literal: Ji returned asked pickled-fish owner; indeed said: "Under garden thatch pile obtained one white fish; substance shape unusually common; to make pickled fish; surpassingly beautiful; therefore to present.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji questioned the donor and learned that under a straw stack in the garden they had found a white fish of odd shape, too fine for ordinary fare—hence the gift."

sentences.zh: 」武庫封閉甚密，其中忽有雉雊。

translations.literal: " Armory sealed closed very tight; within suddenly had pheasant crow.
translations.idiomatic: Though the armory was sealed tight, a pheasant suddenly crowed inside."

sentences.zh: 華曰：「此必蛇化為雉也。

translations.literal: Hua said: "This certainly snake transformed into pheasant."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua said, "A snake must have turned into that bird."

sentences.zh: 」開視，雉側果有蛇蛻焉。

translations.literal: " Opened viewed; beside pheasant indeed had snake slough.
translations.idiomatic: They opened the doors and found a shed snakeskin beside the bird."

sentences.zh: 吳郡臨平岸崩，出一石鼓，槌之無聲。

translations.literal: Wu commandery Linping shore collapsed; produced one stone drum; striking it had no sound.
translations.idiomatic: When the bank at Linping in Wu commandery gave way, a stone drum emerged that rang silent when struck.

sentences.zh: 帝以問華，華曰：「可取蜀中桐材，刻為魚形，扣之則鳴矣。

translations.literal: Emperor used to ask Hua; Hua said: "May take Shu central paulownia wood; carve as fish shape; strike then will sound.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted Zhang Hua, who said, "Carve Shu paulownia into the shape of a fish and strike it—the drum will sing."

sentences.zh: 」於是如其言，果聲聞數里。

translations.literal: " Thereupon as his words; indeed sound heard several li.
translations.idiomatic: They did as he said and the tone carried for miles."

sentences.zh: 初，吳之未滅也，斗牛之間常有紫氣，道術者皆以吳方強盛，未可圖也，惟華以為不然。

translations.literal: At first, Wu's not yet destroyed; between Dipper and Ox often had purple qi; dao technicians all considered Wu side strong flourishing; not yet may plot; only Hua considered not so.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wu fell, a purple vapor lingered between the Dipper and the Ox; every augur blamed Wu's strength—only Zhang Hua disagreed.

sentences.zh: 及吳平之後，紫氣愈明。

translations.literal: When Wu pacified after; purple qi ever brighter.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu surrendered the glow burned brighter still.

sentences.zh: 華聞豫章人雷煥妙達緯象，乃要煥宿，屏人曰：「可共尋天文，知將來吉凶。

translations.literal: Hua heard Yuzhang man Lei Huan subtly comprehended weft stars; then invited Huan lodge; screen people said: "May together seek heaven patterns; know coming good ill.
