translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Lei Huan of Yuzhang read the heavens with uncanny skill, Zhang Hua invited him to stay the night, dismissed the servants, and said, "Let us study the sky together and learn what lies ahead."

sentences.zh: 」因登樓仰觀，煥曰：「僕察之久矣，惟斗牛之間頗有異氣。

translations.literal: " Then ascended tower looked up observe; Huan said: "Servant observed long; only between Dipper Ox rather has strange qi.
translations.idiomatic: From the tower Lei Huan said, "I have watched a long time—something strange rides between the Dipper and the Ox."

sentences.zh: 」華曰：「是何祥也？

translations.literal: " Hua said: "What is this auspicious?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua asked what omen it foretold."

sentences.zh: 」煥曰：「寶劍之精，上徹於天耳。

translations.literal: " Huan said: "Precious sword's essence; upward penetrates to heaven ear."
translations.idiomatic: Huan answered, "It is the aura of a storied blade reaching up to heaven."

sentences.zh: 」華曰：「君言得之。

translations.literal: " Hua said: "Lord's words obtain it."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua said, "You have named it."

sentences.zh: 吾少時有相者言，吾年出六十，位登三事，當得寶劍佩之。

translations.literal: I young time had physiognomist say; my age exceed sixty; position ascend three affairs; ought obtain precious sword wear it.
translations.idiomatic: A fortune-teller once told me that past sixty and risen to the Three High Offices I would gird such a sword."

sentences.zh: 斯言豈效與！

translations.literal: These words how verify with!
translations.idiomatic: Can his prophecy finally prove true?"

sentences.zh: 」因問曰：「在何郡？

translations.literal: " Then asked saying: "In what commandery?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua pressed, "In which commandery does it lie?"

sentences.zh: 」煥曰：「在豫章豐城。

translations.literal: " Huan said: "In Yuzhang Fengcheng."
translations.idiomatic: "At Fengcheng in Yuzhang."

sentences.zh: 」華曰：「欲屈君為宰，密共尋之，可乎？

translations.literal: " Hua said: "Wish bend lord as magistrate; secretly together seek it; permissible?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua asked him to take the magistracy there so they could hunt for it together."

sentences.zh: 」煥許之。

translations.literal: " Huan promised it.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Huan agreed."

sentences.zh: 華大喜，即補煥為豐城令。

translations.literal: Hua greatly rejoiced; immediately supplemented Huan as Fengcheng magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Zhang Hua had Lei Huan appointed magistrate of Fengcheng.

sentences.zh: 煥到縣，掘獄屋基，入地四丈餘，得一石函，光氣非常，中有雙劍，並刻題，一曰龍泉，一曰太阿。

translations.literal: Huan arrived county; dug prison house foundation; entered earth four zhang remainder; obtained one stone case; light qi extraordinary; within had paired swords; together carved inscriptions; one called Dragon Spring; one called Grand E.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengcheng Lei Huan dug beneath the jail four yards down and found a stone coffer blazing with light; inside lay twin swords inscribed Longquan and Tai'e.

sentences.zh: 其夕，斗牛間氣不復見焉。

translations.literal: That evening; between Dipper Ox qi no longer seen there.
translations.idiomatic: That night the aura between the Dipper and Ox vanished.

sentences.zh: 煥以南昌西山北巖下土以拭劍，光芒豔發。

translations.literal: Huan used Nanchang west mountain north cliff below earth to wipe swords; light rays splendid issued.
translations.idiomatic: He polished them with clay from the northern cliff of West Mountain outside Nanchang until they blazed.

sentences.zh: 大盆盛水，置劍其上，視之者精芒炫目。

translations.literal: Large basin held water; placed swords atop it; viewers refined brilliance dazzled eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Set in a basin of water, their glare dazzled the eye.

sentences.zh: 遣使送一劍並土與華，留一自佩。

translations.literal: Sent envoy delivered one sword together earth to Hua; kept one self wear.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhang Hua one sword with a packet of clay and kept the other.

sentences.zh: 或謂煥曰：「得兩送一，張公豈可欺乎？

translations.literal: Someone said to Huan: "Obtain two deliver one; Lord Zhang how may deceive?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone protested, "You found two blades but sent only one—do you cheat Duke Zhang?"

sentences.zh: 」煥曰：「本朝將亂，張公當受其禍。

translations.literal: " Huan said: "Root court about chaos; Lord Zhang ought receive its calamity."
translations.idiomatic: Huan replied, "This dynasty verges on chaos—Zhang Gong will bear the blow."

sentences.zh: 此劍當繫徐君墓樹耳。

translations.literal: This sword ought tie Earl Xu's tomb tree ear.
translations.idiomatic: This sword belongs hung on the tomb tree of the lord of Xu—as in the old tale."

sentences.zh: 靈異之物，終當化去，不永為人服也。

translations.literal: Spiritual strange things; ultimately ought transform depart; not forever for people serve.
translations.idiomatic: Such numinous things slip away in time; they are not meant to serve mortals forever."

sentences.zh: 」華得劍，寶愛之，常置坐側。

translations.literal: " Hua obtained sword; treasured loved it; often placed seat side.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua treasured the blade and kept it at his side."

sentences.zh: 華以南昌土不如華陰赤土，報煥書曰：「詳觀劍文，乃干將也，莫邪何復不至？

translations.idiomatic: Finding Nanchang clay inferior to Huayin's red soil, Zhang Hua wrote Lei Huan: "The inscription marks this as Gan Jiang—why has Mo Ye not appeared?

sentences.zh: 雖然，天生神物，終當合耳。

translations.idiomatic: After Lei Huan died his son Hua, a provincial clerk, carried the sword past Yanping Ford; it leapt from his belt into the river. Divers found no blade—only two patterned dragons many yards long coiling underwater and fled back in terror.

sentences.zh: 須臾光彩照水，波浪驚沸，於是失劍。

translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua and Pei Wei died because others feared them; Xie Xi and Xie Jie perished like sacrificial lambs; Ouyang Jian and others fell though guiltless—the people mourned them all.

translations.literal: Zhuangwu state minister Zhu Dao again went to Prince of Changsha; sought restore Hua nobility rank; vacillated long time.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Dao of Zhuangwu petitioned Prince Sima Yi of Changsha to restore Zhang Hua's titles; the court wavered for years.

sentences.zh: 太安二年，詔曰：「夫愛惡相攻，佞邪醜正，自古而有。

translations.literal: Tai'an second year; edict said: "Now love hate mutually attack; flattering evil ugly upright; from ancient yet have.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tai'an an edict declared: "Love and hate clash; slanderers smear the upright—it has always been so."

sentences.zh: 故司空、壯武公華竭其忠貞，思翼朝政，謀謨之勳，每事賴之。

translations.literal: Former Minister of Works, Duke Zhuangwu Hua exhausted his loyal steadfast; thought wing court governance; counsel-planning merit; each affair relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Late Minister of Works Duke Zhuangwu Zhang Hua gave his full loyalty, steadied the court, and earned trust on every measure."

sentences.zh: 前以華弼濟之功，宜同封建，而華固讓至於八九，深陳大制不可得爾，終有顛敗危辱之慮，辭義懇誠，足勸遠近。

sentences.zh: 華之至心，誓於神明。

translations.literal: Hua's utmost heart; swore to spirits bright.
translations.idiomatic: His devotion was sworn before the spirits.

translations.literal: Hua because attack Wu merit; received noble from late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor ennobled him for conquering Wu.

sentences.zh: 初，陸機兄弟志氣高爽，自以吳之名家，初入洛，不推中國人士，見華一面如舊，欽華德範，如師資之禮焉。

translations.idiomatic: When Lu Ji and his brother first reached Luoyang, flush with pride as scions of a Wu great house, they looked askance at northern scholars—yet one meeting with Zhang Hua felt like reunion with an old friend; they revered his moral stature as pupils honor a master.

sentences.zh: 華誅後，作誄，又為《詠德賦》以悼之。

translations.literal: After Hua executed; composed dirge; also composed "Ode on Virtue" to mourn him.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Hua's execution Lu Ji wrote a dirge and an "Ode on Virtue" in lament.

sentences.zh: 華著《博物志》十篇，及文章並行於世。

translations.literal: Hua authored "Broad Investigate Records" ten chapters; together writings circulated in generation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua wrote ten chapters of Records of Broad Learning; his essays circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 二子：禕、韙。

translations.literal: Two sons: Yi, Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Zhang Yi and Zhang Wei.

sentences.zh: 子禕、韙

translations.literal: Sons Yi, Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Sons: Zhang Yi and Zhang Wei.

translations.literal: Yi courtesy Yanzhong; loved learning; humble respectful had father's manner; passed positions regular attendant cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi, courtesy Yanzhong, loved books and carried his father's modesty, rising to regular attendant cavalry.

sentences.zh: 韙儒博，曉天文，散騎侍郎。

translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei was broadly learned in the classics and astronomy and served as gentleman attendant cavalry.

translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi's son Zhang Yu, courtesy Gong'an, inherited his grandfather's title.

translations.idiomatic: Fleeing south across the Yangzi he became aide to the minister-in-chief and gentleman attendant of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 劉卞，字叔龍，東平須昌人也。

translations.literal: Liu Bian, courtesy Shulong; Dongping Xuchang person.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bian, courtesy Shulong, was a native of Xuchang in Dongping commandery.

sentences.zh: 本兵家子，質直少言。

translations.literal: Originally soldier-family son; straightforward plain few words.
translations.idiomatic: Born to a military household, he was blunt and sparing of speech.

sentences.zh: 少為縣小吏，功曹夜醉如廁，使卞執燭，不從，功曹銜之，以他事補亭子。

translations.literal: Young was county petty clerk; merit officer night drunk going toilet; ordered Bian hold candle; did not obey; merit officer harbored hatred; with other matter supplemented pavilion son.
translations.idiomatic: As a young county clerk he refused to hold a candle for the drunken merit officer at night; the officer nursed a grudge and reassigned him to watch a roadside pavilion on a pretext.

sentences.zh: 有祖秀才者，于亭中與刺史箋，久不成，卞教之數言，卓犖有大致。

translations.idiomatic: A holder of the xiucai degree named Zu drafted a letter to the inspector in the pavilion but stalled; Liu Bian offered a few sentences that gave it striking force.

translations.literal: Xiucai said to county magistrate: "Bian; public office clerk's refined one; why do you say use as pavilion son?"
translations.idiomatic: Zu told the magistrate, "Liu Bian is clerk material for the high offices—why waste him on a pavilion?"

translations.idiomatic: The magistrate asked whether he would study.

sentences.zh: 」即使就學。

sentences.zh: 無幾，卞兄為太子長兵，即死，兵例須代，功曹請以卞代兄役。

translations.idiomatic: Liu Bian followed the magistrate to Luoyang, entered the imperial academy, passed the Classics examination, and became a fourth-rank clerk at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 訪問令寫黃紙一鹿車，卞曰：「劉卞非為人寫黃紙者也。

translations.idiomatic: Someone advised him, "Your gifts suit great affairs, not petty chores—better serve as palace warder."

sentences.zh: 後為吏部令史，遷齊王攸司空主簿，轉太常丞、司徒左西曹掾、尚書郎，所曆皆稱職。
